articles.title: Atlético Nacional presenta a James Rodríguez con un histórico video: "El más grande, al más grande"
articles.standfirst: James Rodríguez en Atlético Nacional: Así fue la presentación oficial del volante con el equipo verdolaga
articles.summary: James Rodríguez en Atlético Nacional: Así fue la presentación oficial del volante con el equipo verdolaga
articles.body: En una jornada histórica para el fútbol colombiano, Atlético Nacional hizo oficial el fichaje del mediocampista y capitán de la Selección Colombia, James Rodríguez. Bajo el imponente lema y video de presentación titulado "El más grande al más grande", el conjunto verdolaga confirmó la incorporación del '10', consolidando una de las transacciones más impactantes en la historia reciente del balompié nacional. Tras casi dos décadas de una destacada trayectoria internacional que lo llevó por clubes de primer nivel en Europa y América, James Rodríguez regresa al país donde inició su camino profesional. El volante cucuteño de 35 años, cuyo debut se dio en sus primeros años con Envigado FC, llega a la institución antioqueña en calidad de agente libre tras finalizar su vínculo con el Minnesota United de la MLS. La negociación, que se venía gestando con absoluta reserva, tomó impulso definitivo luego de que el jugador superara con éxito los exámenes médicos en la ciudad de Medellín. A pesar de los constantes rumores que lo vinculaban nuevamente con el fútbol europeo —incluyendo ofertas del balompié italiano—, la propuesta deportiva e institucional de Atlético Nacional termino inclinando la balanza para concretar su retorno. El anuncio se oficializó mediante un cuidado e imponente video en las plataformas digitales del club. En el material audiovisual, Atlético Nacional resalta el legado de James Rodríguez, repasando pasajes de su carrera con la Selección Colombia y su distinción como referente histórico del deporte en el país, conectándolo de inmediato con la grandeza del palmarés verdolaga. En la producción, la camiseta verdolaga con el histórico número de James fue la gran protagonista, marcando el inicio de una nueva etapa que busca impactar tanto en lo deportivo como en la proyección institucional del equipo de Medellín. La llegada de James Rodríguez representa un salto de calidad indiscutible para la plantilla de Atlético Nacional de cara a los retos en el torneo local y las competiciones internacionales. Para el mediocampista, esta etapa en Medellín le permitirá mantener el ritmo competitivo y la continuidad deseada cerca de casa, tras disputar la Copa Mundial de Fútbol 2026 con la camiseta de la Selección Colombia. Se espera que en los próximos días el club realice una rueda de prensa de presentación oficial ante los medios de comunicación y sus hinchas en el Estadio Atanasio Girardot.

articles.title: Fenerbahce coach Kartal’s resignation refused as bottle thrown in Roma tie
articles.summary: Fenerbahce president refuses Ismail Kartal’s resignation after fan threw bottle at coach in Roma Champions League tie.
articles.body:
Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal quit his role with the Turkish club after a spectator threw a water bottle at his head during his side’s 1-1 Champions League draw with Roma on Thursday – only for his president to reject the resignation minutes later.

The 65-year-old Kartal told a news conference he was leaving “never to ⁠return”, adding that he had taken the decision “to clear the way for the club”.

Immediately afterwards, Fenerbahce president Aziz Yildirim told reporters that Kartal “continues in his role”.

“Some fans threw ‌a bottle at the coach’s head this evening during the game. He is upset about it,” Yildirim said.

“I just spoke to Ismail Kartal. He mentioned the bottle incident and he also complained about being under pressure.”

Asked if Kartal had told him that he would stay, Yildirim ⁠said: “There’s no need for him to ⁠say (openly) that he’d continue. I am his senior, I told him to continue and that’s it. We are a family.”

The Istanbul club said on social media that the person who had thrown a bottle at Kartal had been identified and banned from the stadium.

Kartal, who spent a decade at ⁠Fenerbahce as a player, coached the club in 2014-15, then on an interim basis ⁠in 2021-22 before returning for a ⁠full campaign in 2023-24. He was assistant manager at Fenerbahce the last two times the club won the Super Lig and returned for a ‌fourth managerial spell in June.

Fenerbahce have finished second in the Turkish top flight in the last five seasons and reached ‌the ‌league phase of the Champions League this season for the first time in 18 years.

articles.title: Allan Saint-Maximin: Children 'don't have to accept' being racially abused
articles.summary:
Former Newcastle winger Allan Saint-Maximin says he felt it was important to
speak out after his children were racially abused earlier this year in Mexico.
articles.body:
Allan Saint-Maximin could have stayed quiet.

But the French winger felt it was "important to step up" and speak out after his children were racially abused this year.

"Whatever your colour is, you don't have to accept this," he tells BBC Sport.

Saint-Maximin made it clear on Instagram in January that "hatred and discrimination have no place in our society".

The lengthy post was liked by more than 159,000 people, including former Newcastle United team-mates Kieran Trippier and Joelinton.

The father of four has not gone into specifics.

However, before returning to his homeland to play for Lens, he said "some stuff happened with my kids in the school" during his spell at Mexican side Club America.

"I explained to the kids what happened was not normal and they knew already," he says. "They were not really happy about that.

"I was a bit sad about my son, but in every place there is these type of things, even in France, the country where I am from. As I said to them, it's something they don't have to accept.

"After, when we moved to Lens, it was good but you see some stuff and you are like, 'in every place, there are some things different or some things you are not going to like'.

"If you are waiting for the perfect place, you are wrong."

Saint-Maximin leaves club over racist abuse of his children

'One of the best places I've been with my family'

Club America issued a statement expressing "absolute solidarity" with Saint-Maximin and his family, who had the "support of everyone who is part of this institution".

His team-mates held up a 'No to racism' banner before their game against Necaxa.

"It was not the fault of Club America," Saint-Maximin says. "I have nothing against them, the players or the Mexican people. I love the club. It was one of the best places I've been with my family.

"It's just some random people say some stuff and try to attack your family. You never really know who they support or why they do this, but when this affects your kids there are not many choices to take.

"It was a difficult choice for me and my family, but I take my responsibility because I always say I will never accept stuff like this.

"It was important to show to people, especially in my situation, that I can lose a lot of things, but I will never accept this."

Saint-Maximin joined Lens on a short-term deal in the second half of last season.

He played his part in Lens winning the French Cup for the first time in their 120-year history and finishing second in Ligue 1.

Saint-Maximin had a number of offers in the summer, but decided to move to Major League Soccer side Charlotte.

"My family have always followed me to every single place," he says. "So this time was more of a family choice.

"It was a way for me to give back what they have given to me since I started my career."

Saint-Maximin has linked up with former Aston Villa manager Dean Smith, a "straightforward guy" who is going to "tell you the truth straight away".

One of the club's two 'designated players', , external Saint-Maximin has set out to create a legacy under Smith and help those around him improve.

He also wants to entertain Charlotte supporters.

"To see some robot play doesn't make sense to me," the 29-year-old says.

Saint-Maximin is clearly anything but robotic.

The maverick proved something of a cult figure as Newcastle fought to stay in the Premier League for much of his time at the club.

Saint-Maximin also sampled the highs as a resurgent Newcastle qualified for the Champions League in his final campaign on Tyneside in 2023.

But he was only too aware that staff "could lose their jobs" if they went down.

"When you feel that opportunity, that feeling on your shoulder, you are like, 'this is heavy'," he says.

Saint-Maximin embraced that responsibility after quickly striking up a bond with Newcastle supporters following his move from Nice.

He volunteered at the city's foodbank and even gave fans gifts, including Rolex watches.

"If I was able to give all of my money to them, I would because there is nothing better than the feeling they give you," he adds. "It's something you can't buy, and I've tried to.

"The love they give to you, when I ran with the ball, I had the feeling of people behind me and I ran because of them.

"This feeling is incredible. I wish the same for every single player because they can bring the best out of you."

Saint-Maximin spent four years at Newcastle - the longest stint in his nomadic career - before joining Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli.

He worked with Newcastle 's current head coach, Matthias Jaissle, who took over from Eddie Howe this summer.

Saint-Maximin hopes the German and his staff "have the best possible time" at St James' Park - just as he did.

" Newcastle is my dream club," he says. "I love it from the bottom of my heart. I watch every single game.

"They gave me what no-one gave to me and I'll never forget that. I'm very loyal. I had many opportunities to come to the Premier League, but I didn't because of them."

articles.title: Comparan a Cesc con Cruyff y así responde: "Era lento, poco ágil... Tenía el don del pase y poco más"
articles.standfirst: "Cesc Fábregas es para el Como lo que Johan Cruyff fue para el Barcelona"
articles.summary: "Cesc Fábregas es para el Como lo que Johan Cruyff fue para el Barcelona"
articles.body: Mirwan Suwarso, presidente del Como 1907, declaró a 'Movistar Plus Deportes' que "Cesc Fábregas es para el Como lo que Johan Cruyff fue para el Barcelona". "Esperamos que vaya a más. Nos ha ayudado a llegar hasta aquí, y creo que lo más importante de Cesc es que nos ha enseñado cómo creer, cómo pensar y cómo soñar en grande. Lo está demostrando y creo que es posible si trabajas duro", compartió el empresario y director de cine. Cesc, tras el histórico triunfo del Como en Champions League por 4-1 contra el RB Leipzig, reaccionó a la elogiosa comparación de su presidente con Cruyff: "Muy bonito... Me ha llamado hace un par de horas y me ha dicho 'gracias'". "Somos un club muy joven y hemos dado pasos demasiado rápidos... Pero hay que adaptarse a todo. Yo soy un soñador y he hecho una carrera como futbolista gracias a mi fuerza, que era la mentalidad y de querer superarme siempre. Era lento, no era muy ágil... Tenía el don del último pase y poca cosa más. Ahora intento aportar mi experiencia y valores", declaró el exfutbolista de 39 años, que jugó para F.C. Barcelona, Arsenal, Chelsea, Monaco y Como. Cesc Fábregas es entrenador del Como en 2024, y desde entonces ha logrado un ascenso desde la Serie B, la consolidación en la Serie A y una histórica clasificación para la Champions League. "Cesc ha construido para el club y no para sí mismo y su huella permanecerá para siempre", reconoció Mirwan Suwarso, presidente de un Como que ha pasado en pocos años de competir en Serie C a codearse con la élite europea.

articles.title: El Como de Cesc Fàbregas o el arte de saber cómo gastar
articles.standfirst: Debutaron en Champions con una goleada (4-1) sobre el Leipzig
articles.summary: Debutaron en Champions con una goleada (4-1) sobre el Leipzig
articles.body: Quién sabe si se habrá arrepentido Mirwan Suwarso, presidente del Como 1907, de haber cedido su entrada a algunos de los aficionados históricos del club -los nacidos en 1950 o antes- para permitir que quienes llevan toda una vida siguiendo al equipo pudieran vivir una jornada histórica para la ciudad. Se perdió una exhibición magistral de los chicos de Cesc Fàbregas, que, pese a estrenarse por primera vez en la competición, jugaron desde el primer minuto con la autoridad de quien parece llevar años viviendo noches de Champions League: golearon (4-1) al RB Leipzig. Hasta la grada del estadio Sinigaglia estaba de estreno. Derribada la antigua, la nueva se levantó en apenas dos meses, símbolo perfecto de cómo el Como avanza ya, a todos los niveles, a un ritmo que poco tiene que ver con el resto del fútbol italiano: sobre el césped, en los despachos e incluso en las gradas. Y así, desde las colinas de los Prealpes que se divisan en el horizonte del estadio, si hace apenas unos años se podía echar un vistazo a un partido de la Tercera División italiana, hoy, afinando un poco la vista, se puede contemplar a uno de los equipos con más glamour de Europa dominando un partido de Champions League ante un público en el que conviven aficionados de toda la vida, antiguas leyendas como Thierry Henry y Varane -ambos accionistas del club- y actores de Hollywood dispuestos a disfrutar después del partido de un fin de semana en alguna villa junto al lago. El espectáculo ofrecido en la primera noche de Champions fue digno de un Oscar. Desde los primeros minutos, sin el menor complejo ni respeto reverencial, el Como exhibió su fortísima identidad futbolística y todos los principios que, en apenas unos años, lo han convertido en el proyecto más interesante y en mayor crecimiento del fútbol italiano. Presión alta e intensa, en la que participa todo el equipo, y, sobre todo, secuencias de salida de balón desde atrás que invitan al rival a presionar para atacar después el espacio a sus espaldas con carreras y movimientos constantes. Es, sobre todo, cuando se mueven los futbolistas sin balón cuando el Como se transforma en una orquesta preparada para interpretar una sinfonía vibrante y sin una sola nota desafinada. El primer gol lo firma Martin Baturina, todo un misterio durante los primeros meses de la pasada temporada, cuando la presencia de Nico Paz en su misma posición parecía cerrarle las puertas, pero que terminó explotando como falso extremo, preparado para meterse por dentro e intercambiar constantemente su posición con el argentino. El croata recibe el balón en la derecha, a 50 metros de la portería, se deshace de dos rivales con una finta de cuerpo, puro movimiento de cintura, y un control orientado perfecto. Después lanza a Douvikas al espacio, que intenta devolvérsela hacia el centro; el balón golpea en Baku y vuelve a Baturina, que tropieza, se levanta y, con otra finta, recorta hacia su pierna derecha dejando sentados a dos defensas antes de definir con el interior. Tres goles y dos asistencias en los primeros cuatro partidos de la temporada: ahora mismo es el futbolista más en forma del equipo. El Como sigue produciendo fútbol, ritmo y movimientos perfectamente sincronizados en los espacios. El Leipzig de Demichelis intenta también comportarse como el clásico equipo Red Bull que presiona arriba y busca recuperar inmediatamente, pero es incapaz de seguir las referencias del Como, cuyos futbolistas se mueven por todo el campo y hacen saltar por los aires una y otra vez las marcas rivales. Los otros tres goles de la noche soñada del Como son la mejor representación posible del triunfo del juego colectivo de esta máquina construida por Cesc Fàbregas. El segundo nace de una larga salida de balón desde atrás: todo empieza en Butez, el equipo circula de un lado al otro y finalmente encuentra la izquierda, donde Álex Valle se mete por dentro y conecta con Baturina, el habitual ilusionista de las fintas corporales. El croata conduce con el exterior, se libera de la presión y rompe líneas con un pase vertical genial hacia Douvikas, que gana la posición a Lukeba y define a la espalda de Vandervoordt. Y hablando de historias y de primeras veces, Anastasios Douvikas jugaba hace apenas dos años en el Celta y probablemente jamás habría imaginado convertirse en protagonista de una noche de Champions League. El Como pagó 13 millones de euros por él, Cesc ha sabido potenciar al máximo sus virtudes y la pasada temporada terminó con nada menos que 17 goles. Otra historia que no puede pasar desapercibida es la de Luis Milla, producto del Getafe de Bordalás. Un futbolista que quizá alcanzó su madurez más tarde de lo habitual y que ha terminado debutando en Champions con 31 años. Mientras el resto de clubes italianos dormían, el Como pagó apenas seis millones por él. Anoche fue uno de los mejores sobre el césped. En definitiva, no es simplemente un club que tiene dinero para llevarse algunos de los mejores talentos del mercado -muchos de ellos españoles-. Estamos, sobre todo, ante un club que tiene dinero, sí, pero que lo gasta extraordinariamente bien y que después se ocupa de mejorar a cada uno de sus futbolistas gracias al trabajo de un entrenador excepcional como Cesc Fàbregas. En la segunda mitad también encontró su momento de gloria un Assane Diao regenerado, asistido por Nico después de otra acción coral del Como: control y derechazo ajustado al palo. Esta puede ser la temporada de su definitiva consagración. Las lesiones del último año son lo único que, hasta ahora, le ha separado de dar ese salto de calidad capaz de convertirlo en un futbolista de nivel internacional. Y todavía hubo espacio en el marcador para Maxi Perrone, internacional argentino que la pasada temporada fue uno de los tres mejores futbolistas del Como y que este año incluso sale desde el banquillo. Un detalle que permite entender hasta qué punto ha ganado profundidad la plantilla construida por Suwarso y Cesc. Hace seis años, desde las frías gradas del Sinigaglia, el espectáculo que se ofrecía era el de un partido de la tercera división italiana. Hoy, inversiones importantes, sí, pero sobre todo una planificación quirúrgica sustentada en un proyecto deportivo que ha situado en el centro a un entrenador visionario, han hecho posible transformar aquel espectáculo en un partido de Champions League dominado por el Como. ¿Y saben qué es lo más excitante de todo? Que este Como no tiene límites. El estatus ya no está por conquistar: el Como es hoy uno de los grandes de Italia, juega mejor que nadie y gasta mejor que nadie. La única dificultad será encontrar una entrada en el Sinigaglia. Hay pocas. Difícil imaginar que Suwarso vuelva a ceder la suya. Después de lo de esta noche, probablemente ya se haya arrepentido.

articles.title: FPL gameweek four tips: Sign Cole Palmer or Morgan Rogers or both?
articles.summary: BBC Sport FPL expert Holly Shand looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing FPL managers heading into gameweek four, including whether to captain Erling Haaland or a Chelsea player.
articles.body:
The Fantasy Premier League season is entering week four and plenty of managers will be getting itching fingers, with so many chips at our disposal.

Is it time to play a Free Hit or a Wildcard?

BBC Sport FPL expert Holly Shand looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing FPL managers heading into gameweek four.

Chelsea striker Joao Pedro (£7.7m) is the most-owned player in the game, in 72.5% of sides. Given that Chelsea have scored eight goals already this season, and face promoted Hull City at home next, it feels like the right time to be moving towards a double up on their assets.

Cole Palmer (£9.6m) and Morgan Rogers (£7.6m) came on as half-time substitutes in the Carabao Cup against Leeds United on Wednesday, with Palmer scoring a double including a penalty, and Rogers chalking up three assists.

Palmer has the edge, if you can afford him, given his greater goal threat and penalties.

If you are wildcarding this week, you could also consider a triple-up, but having three attacking players from the same team means they need to score two-plus goals every game to make it worth it.

Should you buy Isak or Gakpo from Liverpool?

Liverpool 's Cody Gakpo (£7.3m) is the most-bought player for gameweek four, with more than 500,000 new owners for the home game against Fulham . However, he failed to make their Champions League squad against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday night with an adductor issue and is now a doubt for this game.

Alternatively, Alexander Isak sits as the second-highest scoring forward in the game, with three goals in the past two gameweeks. When he hits a purple patch he is a formidable threat.

The issue is his £9.1m price tag, making him tough to get to, plus Gakpo has assisted all of his goals, making him the best pick.

I'm a Manchester United fan so I'm perhaps a little biased on this one, but I am hopeful of them getting a result against Manchester City at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon. In Michael Carrick's first league game in charge in January, his side came out the 2-0 victors, with seven wins in eight home league games.

Bryan Mbeumo (£7.9m) was on the scoresheet on that day, with Bruno Fernandes (£12m) chalking up an assist for a 10-point return.

Fernandes is top for shots among all players with 15, while Mbeumo's four big chances is the most of any midfielder in the game. Don't sell them lightly, they are long-term holds.

Who are the key players to buy on wildcard?

I think we've seen enough from the Arsenal defence to invest for the season, with two clean sheets and just one goal conceded. They have conceded just one big chance on their goal, with Ezri Konsa (£4.4m) looking to be a bargain. Double up with David Raya (£6m), Gabriel (£8m) or Riccardo Calafiori (£5.7m).

I'd look to at least double up on Chelsea attackers, with Joao Pedro (£7.7m) in the forward line template and Erling Haaland (£15.5m) perhaps enough from Manchester City right now.

In terms of budget picks, Pascal Gross (£5.6m) could be one of the best to back in the midfield.

Who is the best captain for gameweek four?

If you own Chelsea 's Palmer, then he looks to be the best pick given his routes to points, especially with confirmation in midweek that he remains first choice on penalties.

He leads the way among midfielders for shots in the box with nine.

Chelsea 's home game against Hull City is the standout one to target, so those without Palmer would be advised to look at Rogers or Joao Pedro as viable alternatives.

However, Haaland - away at Manchester United - has five goals in his past three competitive matches and should never be far away from the debate.

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6m) has been a frustrating hold in FPL, with just one goal from the opening three gameweeks, despite having had three big chances.

It's fair to say that he has under-performed, but he has the potential to improve with upcoming home games against Newcastle United and Crystal Palace .

He scored from the bench in the Carabao Cup in midweek so I'll be holding, but there is momentum in the transfer market for other budget picks such as Yoanne Wissa (£6.2m) and Thierno Barry (£5.6m).

I personally don't think there is much to pick between them so would not use a free transfer to swap.

When it comes to budget defenders, Brighton 's Maxime de Cuyper (£4.8m) remains a key pick. He has started the season playing out of position as a winger, where he has racked up one goal and two assists in the opening three gameweeks.

The Seagulls attacking line-up might change, which could see De Cuyper pushed back to full-back, especially when Kaoru Mitoma returns from a hamstring injury.

I think De Cuyper was the one to own in gameweek one, but I'd prefer to buy Arsenal 's Konsa at this price point now.

articles.title: Five things to watch in EFL: High-flying Sheffield Wednesday and boing-ing West Brom
articles.summary: BBC Sport looks at five key talking points before the weekend's Championship, League One and League Two action.
articles.body:
"You stay upright and move forward so long as you keep up the momentum."

Former UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon might not have been talking specifically about the English Football League when he produced that quote, but he's right, success, or failure, in the EFL is just like riding a bike.

Plenty of teams across the 72 have already found their rhythm in the early stages of this campaign but others are seemingly in desperate need of stabilisers.

We have picked out five things to look out for in this weekend's fixtures in the Championship, League One and League Two, including some fascinating reunions with former clubs for some coaches.

West Brom were wobbling all over the place when James Morrison hopped into the saddle in interim charge at The Hawthorns in February.

Albion were second-bottom of the Championship on 11 March but a 10-match unbeaten streak kept them up and, six games into the new season, the Baggies are top of the league.

Wednesday's 1-0 win at Derby - in which Albion played with 10 men for over an hour to secure just a second win at the Rams in 107 years - showcased their change in momentum. It was a ninth clean sheet in 18 league games under Morrison.

They face a stern test of their credentials as QPR head to the West Midlands on Saturday (12:30 BST).

The Hoops, like Albion, have lost only once this season, with that defeat coming against Middlesbrough, and are two points behind the pace-setters in a congested chasing pack.

Julien Stephan's side took just 11 points from their final 13 matches of last season, losing eight of them to finish in 15th, but a summer overhaul seems to have shifted their momentum, despite a mounting injury list.

Pressure grows on Blues managers past and present

Three years can seem a lifetime in football.

At the start of October 2023, John Eustace was Birmingham boss, with his side sixth in the Championship, having guided the turbulent Blues to a 17th-place finish in his first season at St Andrew's.

He was then controversially sacked by City's new American owners to make way for Wayne Rooney.

Eustace enjoyed a successful spell at Blackburn before making the switch to Derby, steering the Rams away from trouble at the end of 2024-25 before making a late run at the play-offs last season.

Wednesday's dismal 1-0 home defeat by 10-man West Brom was a fourth in their opening six games and the natives have become a little restless, despite a troublesome injury list and a failed takeover on the eve of the new campaign.

On Saturday, Eustace welcomes his former club to Pride Park (12:30 BST) with pressure also growing on Chris Davies, who has just started his third campaign in charge at St Andrew's.

Davies took Blues straight back up from League One in record-breaking fashion in his first season at the helm, but expectations have risen, along with the budget, and although they lost for the first time at Norwich on Wednesday , seven points from six matches is an underwhelming return.

A repeat of last season's 1-0 home win for the Rams would make things feel far rosier for Eustace, but far less so for Davies.

Martin aims to arrest the momentum of two clubs

While West Brom are sitting pretty at the top of the Championship, one of the sides who fell short in last season's survival battle were Leicester.

The Foxes are now languishing in 18th in League One, with just five points from their opening five games.

They are already seven points behind leaders Sheffield Wednesday, who won just two games in the Championship last season albeit under exceptional circumstances, and lost their last game 4-0 at home against the other side to come down, Oxford United.

The momentum at the King Power is firmly downwards, but it has to change at some point, right?

On Saturday they travel to Stockport (15:00 BST).

When the Foxes were enjoying their finest hour, winning the Premier League in 2015-16, the Hatters finished ninth in National League North - 125 places below.

Five years ago, when Leicester last played in Europe and finished eighth in the Premier League, County were in the National League.

Both clubs are under new stewardship this season, but Jimmy McNulty has Stockport 15 places higher than Russell Martin's men and Hatters fans will be hoping to continue that momentum in the first league meeting between the sides in 18 seasons.

If you're looking into how momentum changes, then Hillsborough at the start of May, is a good place to start.

The announcement of the takeover of Sheffield Wednesday by a US consortium came moments before the Owls picked up their first win in over seven months - a span of 40 games - beating West Brom on the final day of the 2025-26 season.

Wednesday had suffered the earliest ever relegation in EFL history in February, with 13 Championship games remaining, but they have started with a bang this time around.

Four wins in five games has them top of the pile, with an EFL Cup win over Championship Bolton also highlighting how the tide has turned.

They welcome struggling Wigan Athletic on Saturday (15:00 BST).

After ending last season with one point and no goals in their final three games, the momentum has bled into this season too, the Latics have lost four of their five games so far in League One, plus their EFL Cup tie on penalties.

Gary Caldwell's side have failed to score in three of their past four and the 4-0 home drubbing by local rivals Stockport last time out saw them fall to the bottom of the table on goal difference.

It feels like a case of unstoppable force versus movable object unless Wigan can show they are up for the fight.

Lindsey set to reacquaint himself with Swindon fans

Always nice to meet up with some old faces, isn't it?

Scott Lindsey has the opportunity to do just that as his old team Swindon head to York City on Saturday (15:00 BST).

Lindsey spent two years coaching the Robins' under-18s a decade ago before returning to the club in 2021 as Ben Garner's assistant, then taking the big job himself the following summer after Garner's departure for Charlton.

It lasted just six months, he left in January with promotion-chasing Town sitting outside the play-offs on goal difference, to join Crawley, who were 21st in the same division and he later told the press he felt he never had the backing of Swindon fans.

Lindsey was parachuted in as York boss on the eve of the season after the shock departure of Stuart Maynard and has led the Minstermen to eight points from their opening five games, meaning they could leapfrog second-placed Swindon with a win, while the Robins could go top if they can pick up three points.

BBC Sport will have live text coverage of all the weekend's EFL action, starting with West Ham v Wrexham on Friday, throughout Saturday's fixtures and culminating in Sheffield United v Wolves on Sunday (12:00 BST).

articles.title: La 'amenaza' de Henry al 'MVP' del Como: "De lo contrario no recibirás tu próximo salario"
articles.standfirst: Baturina aseguró que Henry, accionista del Como, era su comentarista favorito de 'CBS'
articles.summary: Baturina aseguró que Henry, accionista del Como, era su comentarista favorito de 'CBS'
articles.body: El debut del Como en Champions League dejó boquiabierto al 'planeta fútbol'. Los de Cesc Fàbregas golearon al RB Leipzig (4-1) con una gran actuación coral... y de Martin Baturina, en particular. El mediapunta croata, a menudo comparado con Luka Modric, se reivindicó con un gol -el primero del Como en la historia del torneo- y una gran asistencia para Douvikas en el 2-0 que le valieron para arrebatar el 'MVP' a Nico Paz o Assane Diao. "Su inteligente juego generó superioridad numérica en el centro del campo, lo que permitió a su equipo dominar el encuentro", aseguró el Grupo de Observadores Técnicos de la UEFA para justificar su elección. "Es increíble haber marcado el primer gol del Como en Champions", reconocía. El ex del Dinamo Zagreb, fichado a cambio de 18 millones de euros hace un año, lo pasó peor delante de los micrófonos de 'CBS Sports Golazo' que en el campo. "Diría que el Barcelona porque son uno de los mejores equipos del mundo y están jugando, creo, el mejor fútbol en este momento. Estoy deseando enfrentarme a ellos", aseguró cuando le preguntaron a cuál de los próximos rivales del Como en Europa (Feyenoord, Manchester United, Lens, AEK, Betis, PSG y Barcelona) le hacía más ilusión enfrentarse. Las complicaciones llegaron cuando Micah Richards le preguntó cuál de los comentaristas del programa era su favorito. "Necesito decir Henry porque es accionista del Como", aseguró el internacional croata. "Por suerte respondiste correctamente, de lo contrario no recibirás tu próximo salario", respondió el propio Thierry Henry, que, de inmediato, con una sonrisa de oreja a oreja, añadió: "Es broma. Calma". "Nunca sabes, necesito ser cuidadoso", replicó Baturina.

articles.title: Laporta: "Este año nos hemos puesto como objetivo ganar Liga, Copa, Supercopa y Champions"
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Barcelona manda un mensaje de ambición en la tradicional ofrenda de la Diada
articles.summary: El presidente del Barcelona manda un mensaje de ambición en la tradicional ofrenda de la Diada
articles.body: Joan Laporta mandó un mensaje de ambición en la tradicional ofrenda al monumento de Rafael Casanova con motivo de la Diada de Catalunya. El presidente del Barcelona se mostró muy feliz por el arranque de la temporada y apuntó a los cuatro títulos como objetivo del club azulgrana este curso. "Este año nos hemos puesto como objetivo ganar Liga, Copa, Supercopa y la Champions y por lo tanto esto te ha de mantener al máximo de concentración y de tensión. Y pensando siempre en el espíritu de equipo, que es lo que tienen que hacer los jugadores y ello nos llevará a ganar títulos", apuntó Laporta ante los medios antes de realizar la ofrenda floral. Preguntado por si la Champions hace especial ilusión, lo tuvo claro. "Todos tenemos una especial ilusión por la Champions y vamos a trabajar duro por intentar ganarla". El presidente del Barcelona tuvo palabras de elogio para Lamine Yamal, que dijo que si no se corriese, no se ganaba. "Tiene una madurez para la edad que tiene que es genial y es muy ilustrativo de lo que tiene que hacer este equipo esta temporada. Con tensión, con intensidad, con compromiso, sin relajarse. Trabajar a tope para ir a por todas", aseguró. Además, Laporta apuntó que se esperaba este gran inicio del Barcelona porque Deco ha hecho una gran plantilla. "Sí me lo esperaba porque tenemos muna plantilla muy compensada. Lo que ha hecho Deco y todo su equipo es que todo el mundo tiene que estar muy atento porque hay mucha calidad en la plantilla. Tenemos dos equipos muy competitivos que juegue quien juegue lo hace bien. Por lo tanto todos tienen que estar muy alerta, comprometidos y en tensión. No cabe la relajación. Teniendo presente que somos candidatos a ganar títulos", explicó el máximo dirigente culé. Laporta, que estuvo acompañado por Fermín en los actos de la Diada, deseó que la dinámica de las goleadas se mantenga pero también apeló a la prudencia. "Hay que tocar de pies en el suelo. Esto solo ha hecho que empezar, esperemos que siga así. La verdad es que lo están haciendo muy bien. Hay un gran nivel y compromiso. Además, eso que decían que este año para ganar hay que correr y jugar con intensidad, lo hacemos. Todos estamos muy ilusionados y hay que seguir con esta actitud", aseveró.

articles.title: Alisson Becker, multado con 8.000 libras por darle una patada a la tablilla del cuarto árbitro
articles.standfirst: El guardameta del Liverpool fue sancionado por la FA tras dañar el panel electrónico de cambios al término del polémico empate ante el Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: El guardameta del Liverpool fue sancionado por la FA tras dañar el panel electrónico de cambios al término del polémico empate ante el Nottingham Forest
articles.body: La Federación Inglesa (FA) ha impuesto una multa de 8.000 libras esterlinas a Alisson Becker por su comportamiento tras el empate 2-2 entre Liverpool y Nottingham Forest. El portero brasileño perdió los papeles al final del encuentro y propinó una patada a la tablilla electrónica de sustituciones situada en la zona del túnel de vestuarios, llegando a dañarla. La acción fue la culminación de una tarde cargada de tensión para el brasileño. Durante la segunda parte, con el marcador igualado, Alisson ya había visto una tarjeta amarilla por protestar al colegiado después de que el cuarto árbitro no tuviera preparado el panel electrónico para realizar una triple sustitución de su equipo. La confusión permitió al Forest reanudar rápidamente el juego, una acción que terminó con un penalti señalado contra el Liverpool tras una entrada del brasileño sobre Neco Williams. Aunque el conjunto de Anfield logró rescatar un punto en los minutos finales, la frustración acompañó a Alisson hasta el pitido final. Las imágenes difundidas en redes sociales mostraron al portero caminando hacia los vestuarios y golpeando con fuerza la tablilla del cuarto árbitro, un gesto que motivó la posterior investigación de la FA. En su resolución, el organismo inglés explicó que se le acusó de haber actuado de forma impropia en la zona del túnel tras el encuentro. Alisson Becker aceptó los cargos y recibió la sanción estándar de 8.000 libras (casi 9.500 euros).

articles.title: UEFA wants FIFA subsidiaries’ blocked from Infantino discovery fight in US
articles.summary: UEFA urges US court to deny FIFA subsidiaries’ bid to join Gianni Infantino discovery fight as president battle rumbles.
articles.body:
UEFA has urged a United States court to reject an attempt by FIFA’s American subsidiaries to intervene ⁠in its bid to obtain evidence for a potential Swiss criminal case against FIFA President Gianni Infantino over his abandoned World Cup commercial rights plan.

In a filing late on Thursday in the Manhattan federal court, European football’s governing body ⁠said FIFA (Americas) Inc and FWC2026 US Inc were improperly trying to act as stand-ins for FIFA and Infantino, neither of whom has sought to join the case.

UEFA said its request under a US discovery law seeks documents and testimony from Thrive Capital Management and its founder Joshua Kushner, who it says may hold information about ‌the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise transaction.

The plan, which Infantino withdrew on August 1 after a backlash from football bodies and other critics, envisaged selling a permanent stake in commercial and operational rights connected to the World Cup and other FIFA events to private investors.

UEFA considering criminal complaint against FIFA’s Infantino

UEFA has said it is considering filing a criminal complaint in Switzerland alleging criminal mismanagement by Infantino and potentially other FIFA officials. Infantino and FIFA have not been charged with wrongdoing.

FIFA accused UEFA last week ⁠of running a “ smear campaign ” and characterised the discovery applications as a fishing expedition ⁠intended to damage FIFA and its leadership.

FIFA did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and Infantino has denied doing anything wrong.

In Thursday’s response, UEFA said the subsidiaries had no direct legal interest in the New York proceedings because they were ⁠not targets of the contemplated Swiss case and were not recipients of the proposed subpoenas.

It said the confidentiality concerns cited by the US subsidiaries belonged, if ⁠to anyone, to their Swiss parent, FIFA. UEFA also argued ⁠that Thrive and Kushner already have lawyers who can challenge any subpoenas after they are served.

Thrive did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Thrive founder Kushner is the brother of Jared Kushner, son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.

UEFA said granting the subsidiaries ‌a role before the court rules would depart from the usual process for requests under Section 1782, which are commonly granted initially without opposition and then tested through motions to quash.

The European body argued that ‌the ‌subsidiaries’ intervention would create unnecessary delay by adding another round of merits briefing before UEFA could seek the records.

The court has not yet ruled on either UEFA’s discovery application or the intervention motion.

Infantino is set to stand for a fourth term in FIFA’s presidential elections in March.

articles.title: Un tridente ofensivo descansado
articles.standfirst: Óskarsson, Barrenetxea y Kubo no tuvieron minutos el lunes en Elche y recibirán frescos a un Atlético de Madrid ante el que podrían volver a ser titulares, sobre todo los dos primeros
articles.summary: Óskarsson, Barrenetxea y Kubo no tuvieron minutos el lunes en Elche y recibirán frescos a un Atlético de Madrid ante el que podrían volver a ser titulares, sobre todo los dos primeros
articles.body: Take Kubo, Orri Óskarsson y Ander Barrenetxea podrían formar este domingo el tridente de ataque de la Real Sociedad contra el Atlético de Madrid, un encuentro que afrontarían descansados, ya que ninguno tuvo minutos el lunes pasado en Elche. La duda está en si Pellegrino Matarazzo contará con los tres o dará continuidad a Luka Sucic en uno de los dos costados, probablemente en el del nipón, con Mikel Oyarzabal de media punta. La Real ha disputado cinco partidos en solamente 18 días, lo que ha llevado a Matarazzo, como contamos ayer en MARCA, a tirar de hasta 24 futbolistas para no quemar ya de inicio a algunos y esos cambios llevaron a que Kubo, Óskarsson y Barrenetxea fueran suplentes el lunes en el Martínez Valero, primero, y no jugasen nada, después. El japonés, el islandés y el donostiarra habían encarado ese encuentro contra el Elche después de ser titulares cuatro días antes frente al Celta y el segundo y el tercero también el anterior fin de semana ante el Espanyol, en los dos partidos disputados hasta la fecha en Anoeta, lo que lleva a pensar que el técnico de Nueva Jersey podría tener en mente de nuevo alinearles de inicio como locales. La duda estaría, si como parece Oyarzabal es media punta como esos dos días, en si Kubo recupera su sitio en el costado derecho del ataque, como contra el Celta, o es Sucic el que se desplaza un poco a esa posición, como frente al Espanyol, y el crack nipón tiene que esperar a salir desde el banquillo. Los que sí parece serán de nuevo titulares casi con toda seguridad son Óskarsson y Barrenetxea, porque ambos han empezado bien la temporada, como muestra que firmaron los tantos del primer triunfo logrado, el 2-1 al Espanyol, además de que en otros partidos se han dejado ver en más ocasiones de ataque de una Real que quiere derrotar este domingo al Atlético para sumar la tercera victoria en LaLiga y acercarse a los puestos continentales, antes de su estreno el jueves en la Europa League.

articles.title: Spurs, Man City and Man Utd face defining Premier League matches this weekend, says Paul Merson
articles.summary: Winless Tottenham take on Everton on Saturday in what will be a big game for Roberto De Zerbi's side and their confidence; the Manchester derby takes place on Sunday; watch Spurs vs Everton and Manchester United vs Manchester City live on Sky Sports this weekend
articles.body:
Spurs are still without a win or a goal in the Premier League after three games and will play against an unbeaten Everton team on Saturday Night Football, live on Sky Sports , in front of their expectant fans.

Meanwhile on Sunday, the Manchester derby takes place as Michael Carrick's inconsistent United team take on a City side facing their first big test in the post-Pep Guardiola era.

Read below for the Magic Man's thoughts on two massive fixtures...

Spurs have to beat Everton this weekend. It's a cup final for them - I'd go as far as to say this is their season on the line.

If they lose to Everton, then you starting thinking: this is going to be another grind of a season. Here we go again. You would start really, really worrying as a Tottenham fan.

But if they go and beat Everton, you start going two games without a defeat, they'll be on four points. Then all of a sudden you can build from there.

It's not as big as the Spurs vs Everton game on the final day of last season. If they lost that game, they were going to Lincoln.

But, at the moment, I just don't see this team putting five or six wins on the trot together. So this is a big football match.

The start Spurs have had is Brentford away, Newcastle at home and Nottingham Forest away. If they lose to Everton and have one point from four games, you start to worry.

If they beat Everton, then they've got every chance of beating Aston Villa at home next week. If they don't beat Everton, they're not beating Villa. That's how it works. It's a snowball effect.

When you win football matches, you expect to win the one after. But if you don't, the confidence goes.

'I still don't see Man Utd in my top five'

Man Utd have got the Manchester derby - and their season is in the balance too. If you beat Man City, you're flying. If you get beat by Man City, here we go again.

It would be one point from two games including the Everton game. And other teams are winning around you.

I've said all along: I don't think Man Utd have bought very well. The squad isn't big enough. It's nowhere near enough.

Defensively they're nowhere near good enough. They let in two goals against Everton - and they were two good goals, but one of them was from the edge of the box. Everybody's behind the ball.

When you're winning, put another forward on. Don't take a forward off and put a defender on. Don't give that team the opportunity.

Instead, if you put a forward on for a midfielder or a forward, it changes the game completely. If you're the other manager, you think: 'Oh no, what am I going to do?'.

Instead, Man Utd just invited pressure on. Just don't do that, especially if you're a big team.

If you're Coventry and you go in front at Everton, you of course put a defender on 100 per cent. But when you're Man Utd, I don't see the need to do that.

If you're dictating the game, Everton don't get that chance for Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

So I am worried - and this is why I didn't put Manchester United in my top five at the start of the season. Nothing's changed for me since then. When you draw games, it hurts you.

'Time to find out how good Man City are'

I don't think Man City have been great. But sometimes I look at teams when they keep winning and they haven't played well as a real worry for the other sides.

Sometimes wins can cover cracks - but City have got Erling Haaland scoring goals. And they kept a clean sheet against Coventry last time out, that's a positive for them.

City have got some big games coming up against Man Utd and Liverpool. That's the test to know where City are under Enzo Maresca.

If City win those two games and the match against Sunderland in between, they're not going to be far off the top come the end of the season.

If they don't get at least two points out of those two games, then Arsenal could run away with the league title a bit. I have Chelsea down for third in the league and they're already miles off Arsenal.

articles.title: How concerned should big-spending Tottenham be after winless and goalless start to Premier League season?
articles.summary: Spurs are yet to win or score in the Premier League this season despite a big summer of spending; Roberto De Zerbi's side also failed to have a shot on target last weekend; watch Tottenham vs Everton on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Premier League from 5pm; kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
Last weekend's 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest saw Spurs fail to have a shot on target for the first time in a league game in over four years as they battled to their first point of the season.

Roberto De Zerbi's new-look side are yet to click after a £332m summer outlay which saw 10 new players arrive.

Having made their worst start to a league season since 2008, Spurs go in search of their first victory on Saturday as they host Everton, live on Sky Sports ​​​​​​.

Here, Sky Sports News' Tottenham reporter Michael Bridge answers your questions, while we also look at the stats behind their start and hear your thoughts on their opening three league games...

"I'm not concerned. It's only three games, and Spurs would've taken a draw at Nottingham Forest. It's a hard place to go under a very good manager in Oliver Glasner.

"I was at the Brentford game where Spurs were well beaten. I can fully appreciate that Tottenham being under-prepared is unacceptable, so I'll flip it round and say Brentford gave Spurs a good hiding and they fully deserved their win.

"Newcastle could have gone either way, but Spurs weren't clinical enough. But the reason why I'm not concerned is that it's still so early in the season.

"The last three games have shown me a little bit of a realisation that you can't expect it all to click so quickly when there have been so many incomings and departures."

"De Zerbi absolutely did not have any complaints about the medical team. He's working closely with the medical team.

"Let's not forget that in the last couple of seasons Spurs have suffered an injury crisis, with key players missing an entire season.

"Tottenham Hotspur have worked hard over the last few months to ensure that this doesn't happen again, including an investigation which looked into whether the pitch had a bearing on such serious injuries.

"To clarify, De Zerbi doesn't want to take players off at certain minutes, but he's instructed to do so by his medical staff.

"He's not challenging them or being divisive. He's working alongside them. They are ensuring that De Zerbi has these players for the long term to hopefully prevent situations like Mohammed Kudus and James Maddison from occurring again."

"If it wasn't for De Zerbi, there'd have been a very high chance Tottenham would be in the Championship right now.

"Spurs have given De Zerbi the keys to mould the squad how he sees fit. I'm of the opinion that he has earned the right to have those keys.

"He has made tough decisions, including allowing Luka Vuskovic to go to Brighton and to bring in Jan Paul van Hecke for a big fee despite him having a year to go on his contract.

"I must reiterate, it's three games in. For me, the start of the season for Spurs can be seen as post-transfer window.

"I think we won't see the real Spurs until maybe even November because there have been so many changes: new captain, new forward line, new midfield, new defence. It takes time."

"With the outlay, you have to expect that they must finish in European places.

"It won't be made public, but the aim must be to get back into Europe.

"Now, of course, when I say Europe, ideally it's the Champions League. But even if it was Europa League football, people are now more aware than ever that additional home fixtures generate revenue.

"Brad, in my personal view, mid-table is the very least they should be aiming for."

Spurs are aiming to avoid unwanted history on Saturday - if Everton keep a clean sheet, then it will be the first time Tottenham have failed to score in their first four league games of a season.

Their struggles in front of goal are a result of a lack of quality chances created.

Despite ranking mid-table for shots attempted in the Premier League this season, Spurs are bottom for expected goals (xG) per shot, as you can see below.

Spurs' overall xG is the third lowest, while only Coventry have underperformed their chances more than Spurs, which you can see below.

Since the start of last season, the average xG per game by a Premier League side is 1.41, but Spurs are yet to reach that average return for xG in any game under De Zerbi.

One of the Italian's issues has been a lack of consistency in his attacking selections. De Zerbi has started with three different attacking combinations in all three league games this season and has used 10 different starters across his front three in his 10 league games in charge.

And it is not just the front line where De Zerbi has faced selection issues. Tottenham have made eight changes to their starting XI in the Premier League this season, the most of any side and their joint-most in the first three games of a campaign in the competition.

Spurs' running stats are another alarming area of concern this season.

Tottenham were only outrun once in De Zerbi's seven games in charge last season as they dramatically escaped relegation on the final day. This season, however, Spurs have been outrun in every game.

In fact, they rank second-bottom for distance run and 16th for sprinting distance in the Premier League this season, having been in the top five under De Zerbi last season.

Higher physical output, improved threat and better attacking quality are all needed to kickstart their season.

RichN: I think it's mad to expect a team with nine or 10 new players, nearly all first 11 players, to gel straight away. It'll take time. Also, still having our previous most creative players in Kudus, Kulusevski, Simons and Maddison either still out or not match fit is a huge handicap for De Zerbi.

Russ K: After the money that has been spent on assembling De Zerbi's 'Dream Team', we should have made a stronger start than what we have. No goals in the first three games is a real cause for concern. We need a goal scorer, and for me, Troy Parrott would have been an excellent addition.

Mitch L: Not too concerned at all; can see improvement at times game by game. Forward line just needs to click and will come in time. Savio is refreshing to see, very direct and will get us goals through his play. Think one or two goals and confidence is back, and we see them kick on.

dbuk1: It's not concerning at all. We have had a big turnaround of players for the first time in my living memory at Spurs. It's been three games, and we still haven't got a fully fit squad. Everyone calm down and give it time! LF: Not concerning at all. We have signed a number of players who need time to gel. We also have a number of players still returning from long-term injuries who, once fit, will bolster the squad. Mikel Arteta had five to six seasons to get Arsenal where they are now, so give De Zerbi time!

THFC-TrustTheProcess: In the first two games, we were missing attacking players. Savio, Maddison and Kulusevski all out, and Kudus only on the bench after missing pre-season. The expected goals in the last game were miles better than what we produced for most of last season. Just need to start taking our chances. No need to panic yet!

SLB110890: I said when we had Frank, Rome wasn't built in a day! We have 10 new players and got rid of a load of players who only managed to help us just about avoid relegation. To get all those players to gel instantly is unrealistic; be patient and let the Italian build Rome.

Jmzrc: I support Brighton, so I'm familiar with De Zerbi's approach. As Lewis Dunk has said, it took time for players to work out the system and what was expected, but when they did, we were flying. De Zerbi is a system manager, so I think Spurs will be strong once the new players bed in. Be patient.

Imran: The lack of creativity in the team concerns me. Any player with it is injured. Can't see Spurs scoring enough goals

Steven Davids: To make so many changes in a short space of time and expect instant results isn't realistic. Patience and support are what the club needs. Better results and performances will come. Hadcarr: It's concerning but not surprising. A group of individuals will take time to gel into a team. All Spurs can hope for this season is mid-table.

Dwilliams: At the moment I'm not too overly concerned. Yes, the lack of attacking threat in the last few games hasn't been ideal. Let's not forget that this time last season we had beaten Man City 2-0 and were near the top, so a lot can change.

Bravo31: We don't seem any better than last season, defence unsure, no midfield flair or aggression, and no one as an out-and-out goal scorer. Concerned!!

timm900: It's far from an ideal start, especially considering how much money has been spent, but with the amount of players that have been brought in, it's bound to take a little time to gel. If it hasn't markedly improved after 10 games, then it's time to panic.

articles.title: Newcastle: Lewis Hall signs new contract until 2031
articles.summary: Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall signs a new contract with the club that runs until 2031.
articles.body:
Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall has signed a new contract with the club that runs until 2031.

The left-back, who has been the subject of interest from Manchester United , has agreed a two-year extension to his original deal.

Hall said it was a "really proud moment" to extend his stay as a boyhood supporter of the club.

"It's an absolute pleasure to play for this club and to represent the supporters," he said. "I know how much it means to them.

"To be able to bring joy to their faces, it's a big thing for me. I obviously have a family connection with the club, which is incredibly important to us all.

"One of the main reasons I play is to make my family proud, and I know how much it means to them to watch me playing for Newcastle United .

"It's a really good place to be. It's really pleasing with how we've started the season, especially with the new gaffer [Matthias Jaissle] and coaching staff coming in, and I think we can go on to achieve really big things."

Hall, 22, has made 106 appearances for Newcastle since joining the club from Chelsea in 2023.

Jaissle said the defender is a "very important player for us and for what we are building here".

"His mentality is exactly what you want in a young player," he said. "He wants to learn every day and he wants to be better in every match.

"Lewis covers ground in a way that few players can. He defends with maturity and intelligence, and his technical level means he can support the team higher up the pitch.

"What excites me most is that I believe the best is still to come from Lewis. He has a lot of room to develop, and I am looking forward to working with him as he grows with us."

Analysis - Newcastle strengthen position with extension

This has been a busy summer at Newcastle - both in terms of ins and outs - but tying Hall down is a particularly significant move.

It was just last month that Jaissle replied "no chance" when Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel informed him that his former side were looking at Hall.

This deal further strengthens the club's position.

It also rewards Hall for his development since he arrived from Chelsea as a raw left-back three years ago.

Hall has worked on the defensive side of his game and, on his day, proved he is capable of even keeping Barcelona star Lamine Yamal quiet from open play in the Champions League.

He has been a real outlet going forward for Newcastle , too, and has already set up two goals this season.

That should not come as a huge surprise.

Of those full-backs to play a minimum of 900 minutes across the Premier League last season, Hall led the way for high-speed runs and underlapping runs per game. He also ranked in the top three for dribbles completed per match.

It feels like there is a lot more to come from him as he looks to get back into the England squad after missing out on the World Cup.

articles.title: La redención de Prestianni, de su sanción histórica a salirse sin Mourinho: "Está arrasando"
articles.standfirst: Suma siete goles y dos asistencias en los siete partidos que ha jugado con Benfica este curso
articles.summary: Suma siete goles y dos asistencias en los siete partidos que ha jugado con Benfica este curso
articles.body: Gianluca Prestianni (Ciudadela, 2006) tocó fondo en la derrota ante el Real Madrid (0-1) el 17 de febrero. "Le llamó cinco veces mono a Vinicius", aseguró Kylian Mbappé. A la UEFA no le tembló el pulso y sancionó al extremo argentino del Benfica con seis partidos de suspensión -tres de ellos condicionados- por “conducta discriminatoria de carácter homófobo”. Sin embargo, el ex de Vélez, fichado en 2024 a cambio de 9 millones de euros, se ha redimido a lo grande en este inicio de curso. Acumula siete goles y dos asistencias en los siete partidos que ha disputado. Goles, golazos en su mayoría, a cada cual mejor. "Mourinho me dio mucha confianza, no sé si reaccioné demasiado tarde. Esta temporada tengo muy claro lo que quiero hacer. Hablé con Marco Silva y le dije que mejoraría mucho en estadísticas individuales, goles y asistencias. Por ahora lo estoy consiguiendo y espero seguir así", reconoce el internacional argentino. En su despegue definitivo ha habido un aspecto clave. Su cambio de banda. Ha pasado de la izquierda a la derecha y sus eslalon, jugando a pierna cambiada, están causando un 'roto' tras otro: "Me siento más cómodo jugando de extremo izquierdo. El míster me está dando la oportunidad de jugar en esa posición, y trato de demostrar en cada partido que puedo jugar ahí con más frecuencia". "Estoy feliz. Intento demostrar lo que sé y lo que puedo hacer. Es un paso más allá”, reconoce Prestianni. Marco Silva, sin embargo, prefiere 'desvincularse' de su 'metamorfosis'. "Tiene 20 años y ha pasado por momentos difíciles. Él tiene mucha calidad y tenemos que aprovecharlo. Hablé con él sobre la necesidad de mejorar sus estadísticas, pero eso es mérito suyo", admitía el nuevo técnico del Benfica a 'Sport TV'. Por su parte, el presidente Rui Costa aprovechó para 'sacar pecho': "No hace mucho pocos le daban crédito. Nosotros terminamos dándole crédito siempre, por eso lo trajimos. Ahora está arrasando, también debido a su crecimiento, el tiempo que ha pasado en el club, el tiempo que ha pasado en Europa y su edad, que le está ayudando a estar donde está. Prestianni es claramente otro jugador que queremos conservar, no hay duda de eso". "Tengo contrato con el Benfica hasta 2029 y voy a dar la vida por el club", asegura Prestianni, que, en el mercado invernal, antes de su polémico episodio con Vinicius, estuvo muy cerca de 'hacer las maletas' y abandonar Da Luz. Lo evitó José Mourinho. "River Plate intentó ficharme del Benfica. Fue una conversación entre los clubes. Pero hablé con Mourinho, me preguntó qué quería hacer. Trabajo cada día para aprovechar las oportunidades y, gracias a esa conversación, me quedé en Europa. Quiero triunfar allí", confesó a 'Velez 670 Radio'. Es más, el extremo del Benfica le está eternamente agradecido al ahora técnico del Real Madrid: "Tuve la suerte de tenerlo como entrenador. Siempre intenta que te superes. Está un poco loco, pero en el buen sentido [ríe]. Le deseo lo mejor. Me ayudó a crecer muchísimo, tanto en ataque como, sobre todo, en defensa. La defensa era muy difícil para mí y me ayudó a convertirme en un jugador más completo". Un 'cóctel' que está dando sus frutos. "Prestianni es, en estos momentos, el elemento más desequilibrante del Benfica", afirma Paulo Catarro en 'Now'. La redención ha comenzado.

articles.title: Edson Alvarez: West Ham and Mexico midfielder denies kidnapping accusation
articles.summary: West Ham and Mexico midfielder Edson Alvarez posts a statement on social media denying the allegation made by film producer Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez.
articles.body:
West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez has denied accusations he was involved in the alleged kidnapping of a film producer in Mexico.

Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez told Mexican publication TV Notas , external that he was forced into a vehicle at gunpoint in the Polanco district of Mexico City in 2024 by the family of Alvarez's former father-in-law Jonathan Toache Bedolla.

Ordonez, who claims Alvarez was not directly involved in the kidnapping but was aware of the plot, says he was commissioned to make a documentary about the footballer's life and was owed £150,000 for the project.

Alvarez, who made his Mexico debut in 2017, issued a statement on his social media to deny the allegations and says he will consider legal action.

"I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me," Alvarez, who is also Mexico's captain, posted on social media.

"Over the past several months, my name and image have repeatedly been used to generate greater media attention around a situation that has nothing to do with me.

"Until now, I had chosen not to respond. However, there are limits, and attributing knowledge, responsibility, or involvement in matters of this nature to me without presenting a single piece of evidence clearly crosses that line."

He added that the media outlets were prioritising "sensationalism" instead of "accuracy and truth" and said he would keep focusing on his family and his career.

Alvarez has made 74 appearances for the Hammers since joining from Ajax in 2023, but has only featured once so far this season, against Portsmouth in the Carabao Cup.

articles.title: El cromo de Futre que a Casillas le faltaba para completar su colección y que 'no existe'
articles.standfirst: El exmadridista habló de la etapa en la que coleccionaba cromos, a principios de los 90
articles.summary: El exmadridista habló de la etapa en la que coleccionaba cromos, a principios de los 90
articles.body: Iker Casillas fue uno de los protagonistas del acto de presentación del álbum de LaLiga este miércoles. El portero estuvo acompañado de Johan Mojica, Álvaro García y Javier Tebas en la sede de LaLiga, y contó alguna anécdota de cuando coleccionaba cromos, a principios de los 90. "Era cuando empezaba el momento más 'friqui' de los niños. Empezabas a descubrir las caras de muchos jugadores. Ponías cara a Poyatos, al Tato Abadía. Cuando arrancaba el periodo escolar te dejaban unos sobres y era el anzuelo para seguir tú buscando más sobres", comenzó explicando Iker. "Me he enfrentado a muchos de ellos. Pasas de estar viéndolos en la tele a convivir en el día a día. Pasas de ese sueño que tenías de pequeño de buscar su firma, a jugar con ellos. Cuando estabas en la cantera buscabas los cromos que faltaban. En la 91-92 había un cromo de Futre y Chendo muy bonito, que era el que faltaba. Yo tiraba más hacia los del Madrid". Detengámonos en ese cromo que dice Casillas que le faltaba de la temporada 91-92, que en realidad es de la colección de la 92-93, aunque la foto sí que se tomó en la temporada 91-92. Casillas habla de un cromo de Futre y Chendo, seguramente influido por los duelos que mantuvieron el extremo del Atlético y el lateral del Real Madrid en aquellos años. Chendo era el marcador de Futre en los derbis. Pero quien realmente sale en el cromo con Futre no es Chendo sino Luis Milla, el padre del actual jugador del Como. La imagen es de un derbi disputado en la 91-92, en la que Futre y Milla se enfrentaron hasta tres veces, dos en LaLiga y una en la final de Copa en el Bernabéu. La colección, eso sí, es del álbum de la 92-93. Lo que no aclaró Casillas es si finalmente pudo conseguir aquel cromo para terminar la colección. No el cromo de Futre con Chendo, sino el cromo de Futre con Milla.

articles.title: Dro, la joya que decepcionó a Flick y deslumbra a Luis Enrique en el PSG: "Es increíble que juegue así"
articles.standfirst: Dro Fernández, centrocampista gallego internacional con España en categorías inferiores, da destellos de su calidad en el PSG tras salir del Barcelona
articles.summary: Dro Fernández, centrocampista gallego internacional con España en categorías inferiores, da destellos de su calidad en el PSG tras salir del Barcelona
articles.body: Dro Fernández, el joven futbolista que dejó el F.C. Barcelona con los 18 años recién cumplidos para fichar por el PSG decepcionando a Hansi Flick, empieza a brillar en el equipo de Luis Enrique. El centrocampista gallego fue titular por primera vez en Champions League en la goleada por 6-1 del PSG ante el Slovan Bratislava. "Sólo tiene 18 años y es increíble que ya esté jugando así. Ya lo conocíamos antes de que se uniera al equipo. Me encanta ver cómo va mejorando. Si sigue jugando así, tendrá oportunidades", dijo Luis Enrique sobre el de Nigrán en la rueda de prensa posterior al partido. Dro Fernández, que ha firmado por el PSG hasta 2030, reconoció tras el partido que "no esperaba jugar, pero hay que estar preparado para cuando llegue el momento y poder ayudar al equipo". "Estoy mucho mejor y con mucha más confianza, que eso lo noto mucho. Pero bueno, con estos compañeros es muy fácil jugar y te lo hacen todo mucho más sencillo. Creo que puedo seguir mejorando y que tengo mucho margen de mejora, y esperemos siga siendo así", analizó. La pasada temporada Dro sumó 685 minutos repartidos en 12 partidos, en los que tuvo tiempo de marcar un gol. En el presente curso el ex del Barcelona, que le dio la asistencia a Fabián para el sexto gol del PSG, lleva disputados 127 minutos en 4 partidos. "Mi objetivo es seguir ayudando al equipo en los momentos que pueda y estar siempre preparado. Quiero seguir creciendo. No tengo prisa ninguna. Estoy muy contento aquí", compartió.

articles.title: El Betis apunta por encima de las cuentas de LaLiga
articles.standfirst: Su victoria a domicilio para arrancar la Champions invita a pensar que mejorará la previsión
articles.summary: Su victoria a domicilio para arrancar la Champions invita a pensar que mejorará la previsión
articles.body: El Betis tiene motivos para pensar que su nuevo límite de coste de plantilla, fijado esta semana por LaLiga en 142,8 millones de euros, puede tener todavía recorrido al alza durante la temporada. Buena parte de los ingresos que sustentan esta cifra dependen de la participación de los verdiblancos en la Champions, para la que la patronal ha realizado una estimación bastante prudente: cinco puntos en las ocho jornadas de la fase de liga y un 27º puesto que dejaría al equipo de Pellegrini fuera del playoff. Una previsión que contrasta bastante con la que maneja internamente el club verdiblanco. Los de las Trece Barras han sido algo más optimistas al confeccionar sus presupuestos y, como avanzó ABC, contemplan terminar la fase de liga alrededor de la 21ª posición, dentro de los 24 primeros y, por tanto, con acceso al playoff previo a los octavos de final. Una diferencia que podría traducirse en nuevos ingresos, tanto por posición como por el millón extra por pasar a las eliminatorias, y con ellos, en más margen para el coste de plantilla. El Betis, de hecho, ha empezado apuntando por encima de las cuentas de LaLiga. Su victoria frente al Lille en la primera jornada el pasado martes, sobreponiéndose hasta en dos ocasiones a un marcador adverso y completando su remontada con un golazo de Troy Parrott, le ha permitido sumar de una tacada tres de los cinco puntos que la patronal estima que conseguirá durante toda la fase de liga. Es decir, en apenas uno de los ocho partidos ya ha alcanzado el 60% de la puntuación utilizada como referencia en las previsiones. El criterio seguido por LaLiga tiene que ver con la ausencia del Betis de la máxima competición continental durante más de dos décadas (su primera y única participación hasta esta temporada 2026-27 fue en el curso 2005-06). La patronal debe establecer una estimación de los ingresos que puede generar el club en Champions y, para ello, utiliza como referencia el comportamiento reciente de otros equipos españoles en circunstancias similares. Así lo explicó ayer Javier Tebas al ser cuestionado específicamente por el caso del conjunto verdiblanco: "El límite que tiene el Betis por entrar en Champions es la media de los equipos que han entrado en los últimos años. Si el año que viene vuelve a estar ya sería otra cosa...". Entre las referencias utilizadas están las recientes participaciones del Girona y el Villarreal, clubes sin una presencia continuada en la Champions. El primero sumó tres puntos y terminó 33º en la temporada 2024-25, mientras que el conjunto castellonense logró un punto y fue 35º un año después. LaLiga mejora esas cifras para el Betis teniendo en cuenta, entre otros factores, su trayectoria europea reciente, hasta proyectarle cinco puntos y aproximadamente una 27ª posición. El resultado de ese cálculo es un escenario en el que los heliopolitanos quedarían eliminados al finalizar las ocho jornadas. Bastante por debajo, por tanto, del que contempla el propio Betis en sus presupuestos, con ese 21º puesto que le permitiría disputar el playoff. El rendimiento en la Champions tiene una incidencia importante en las cuentas. Cada victoria en la fase de liga supone 2,1 millones de euros y cada empate, 700.000 euros más, a los que se añaden los ingresos vinculados a la posición final en la clasificación y los premios correspondientes a cada eliminatoria que se vaya superando. Acceder al playoff proporciona además un nuevo ingreso y garantiza otro partido como local, con la correspondiente taquilla. Por eso, superar la previsión utilizada inicialmente por LaLiga puede terminar teniendo reflejo en el margen económico del Betis. Javier Gómez, director general corporativo de la patronal, dejó abierta ayer esa posibilidad: "Conforme vayan pasando partidos, si va ganando partidos irá aumentando sus ingresos. Eso ya depende. Nos acogemos a los números, ojalá ganen más equipos españoles". El nuevo Límite de Coste de Plantilla Deportiva publicado por LaLiga sitúa al Betis en 142,847 millones de euros, más de 20 millones por encima de los 122,1 que tenía asignados anteriormente. Un importante crecimiento que permite a los verdiblancos mejorar dos posiciones respecto a anteriores publicaciones y los coloca con el quinto mayor límite de Primera división, únicamente por detrás de Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atlético de Madrid y Villarreal. La cifra permite al club encajar el esfuerzo realizado durante el mercado y el coste de una plantilla reforzada, entre otros, con Dani Ceballos y, en especial, Troy Parrott, cuyo fichaje se disparó hasta 16 millones de euros fijos y cuatro en variables. Pero puede no ser definitiva. Si el Betis cumple su propia previsión europea y termina entre los 24 primeros, los ingresos de Champions estarán por encima del escenario utilizado por LaLiga y podrían proporcionar más margen en posteriores actualizaciones del límite. De momento, la primera jornada ya ha reducido considerablemente la distancia. LaLiga hizo sus cuentas con cinco puntos en ocho partidos y un Betis fuera del playoff. Los verdiblancos llevan tres de tres y en sus propios números miran más arriba: hacia el 21º puesto y una Champions que se prolongue, al menos, una eliminatoria más. Las próximas citas en el torneo, ante Oporto, Feyenoord y Dortmund, tal vez sirvan para superar las previsiones y empezar a soñar con unos cruces del máximo torneo continental que club nunca ha disputado.

articles.title: Lewis Hall: Newcastle United left-back signs long-term contract at St James' Park
articles.summary: Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall has penned a new long-term deal at St James' Park; the England international had been attracting interest from Man Utd; Hall joined the Magpies from Chelsea in August 2023 and since made 107 appearances; his original deal had three years left on it
articles.body:
The England international has committed to a new deal at St James' Park despite Manchester United showing an interest in him during the summer transfer window following the departure of several other key players from the club.

The 22-year-old left-back joined the Magpies from Chelsea in August 2023 and since made 107 appearances for the club, including playing in every round of their successful 2024/25 Carabao Cup campaign - their first domestic trophy in 70 years - only to miss the final with injury.

Hall says the new deal comes as a proud moment.

He told the club's website: "I'm absolutely delighted. It's a really proud moment. It's an absolute pleasure to play for this club and to represent the supporters. I know how much it means to them.

"The fanbase and the support we get here, whether it's at St. James' Park or away, it's the best in the league in my opinion. To be able to bring joy to their faces, it's a big thing for me.

"I obviously have a family connection with the club, which is incredibly important to us all. One of the main reasons I play is to make my family proud, and I know how much it means to them to watch me playing for Newcastle United.

"It's a really good place to be. It's really pleasing with how we've started the season, especially with the new gaffer and coaching staff coming in, and I think we can go on to achieve really big things."

Hall has played every single minute this season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle, including three Premier League games and both wins in the Carabao Cup.

Jaissle said: "I have been impressed with Lewis since I arrived. He is a very important player for us and for what we are building here, so this is exciting news.

"The combination of his ability and his profile make him an ideal fit for our squad, and his mentality is exactly what you want in a young player. He wants to learn every day and he wants to be better in every match.

"Lewis covers ground in a way that few players can. He defends with maturity and intelligence, and his technical level means he can support the team higher up the pitch.

"What excites me most is that I believe the best is still to come from Lewis. He has a lot of room to develop, and I am looking forward to working with him as he grows with us."
