articles.title: Terzic y la metamorfosis del Athletic
articles.standfirst: Se ha metido en el bolsillo a San Mamés con una vistosa propuesta de juego • El vestuario responde a la exigencia y el equipo quiere volar en el primer año del alemán en al Liga
articles.summary: Se ha metido en el bolsillo a San Mamés con una vistosa propuesta de juego • El vestuario responde a la exigencia y el equipo quiere volar en el primer año del alemán en al Liga
articles.body: Elche, Levante y Alavés son las siguientes estaciones del nuevo Athletic de Edin Terzic, un equipo que después de perder sus dos primeros partidos de Liga ante Sevilla y Barcelona ha sacado con nota los compromisos frente a Celta y Atlético. El duelo ante el conjunto de Simeone le dejó bendecido en San Mamés. El preparador alemán (Menden, 43 años) disfruta con lo que tiene entre manos y no ha dudado en trasladar a sus allegados su satisfacción por equipo, afición y entorno. Está más que satisfecho con el desempeño diario de sus futbolistas porque además siente que ésto no ha hecho más que empezar. Entrenar al Athletic después de Valverde, por muchos años el técnico que más partidos ha dirigido en la historia del club, no es sencillo. Terzic lo sabía desde que conoció la propuesta de la Junta Directiva y desde el mismo momento que analizó la posibilidad se puso a trabajar en la idea. El trabajo que desarrolla ahora con sus jugadores viene de atrás puesto que antes de empezar los entrenamientos había mantenido varias charlas con los internacionales y también con los cedidos a los que quería en el grupo para su primer verano en el club. Su llegada a Lezama no fue a puerta fría. El alemán apuesta por el Athletic, por el que firmó después de haber recibido varias ofertas con las que cortar el parón de dos años sin entrenar tras salir del Borussia de Dortmund. Paciencia y minuciosidad forman parte de su agenda. Cuando en noviembre de 2017 se acabó su relación con el West Ham, donde ejercía como asistente de Slaven Bilic, Terzic recibió la llamada de un club de la Segunda División de Alemania con la ilusión de Bundesliga. Lo que para otro asistente con vocación de ascender de rango habría sido una oportunidad para Terzic fue un dilema. Debía aclarar qué quería ser en el fútbol y en los banquillos. Potenció su formación al tiempo que escribía su diario de actuación, que es un documento vivo al que incorpora reflexiones, y se puso en el camino de primer entrenador, aunque su siguiente trabajo fue como asistente. En ese último paso hacia la responsabilidad absoluta del banquillo habló con Bilic para compartir el desarrollo que había realizado. Y éste no lo dudó: ¡Adelante!. Igual que filósofos y pensadores de la talla de Heráclito de Efeso, Hegel o Nietzche fundamentaron teorías alrededor del conflicto, Terzic suma en el Athletic también a partir de esa condición. “Creo en los conflictos para salir de la zona de confort. Hay una línea muy final entre el conflicto y lo que supone perder un vestuario. Considero que tiene mayor valor una buena disciplina más que la motivación”, destacó tiempo atrás al analizar su modelo en The Coaches Voice. La base táctica de su trabajo depende también de una excelente relación con la plantilla, que en el fondo es la herramienta del éxito. El discurso de Terzic ha entrado a fuego en un vestuario al que no le cuesta cantar que cree en su entrenador. De la misma manera el entrenador se considera agradecido porque la confianza y creencia es mutua. El entrenador ha enriquecido a su equipo desde la agresividad, el ritmo, el ataque en oleadas y una sucesión de matices e intervencionismo para conseguir la máxima incomodidad en el contrario. Lo ha hecho con la seguridad de que se siente respaldadísimo por el vestuario. La flexibilidad táctica que ha ofrecido en cada partido se sustenta desde la voluntad y receptividad de la plantilla. Esa unívoca disposición del grupo es un matiz que resalta el entrenador y realza las opciones de juego y clasificatorias de los leones. Y el líder de la estructura no se cree la estrella: “No es mi Athletic, no es el de Terzic. Es el Athletic de todos, el que la gente quiere ver”.

articles.title: Tchouaméni, una cuestión de equilibrio
articles.standfirst: Mourinho y su staff celebran la vuelta del francés, que ofrece un perfil diferente a los disponibles hasta ahora
articles.summary: Mourinho y su staff celebran la vuelta del francés, que ofrece un perfil diferente a los disponibles hasta ahora
articles.body: Aurélien Tchouaméni se estrenó en la temporada 26-27 el pasado martes, ante el Inter. Hasta ese momento, José Mourinho no había podido contar con el internacional francés, que acabó lesionado la Copa del Mundo y regresó así al Madrid. Sin ser una opción ni durante la pretemporada ni durante el arranque de la Liga, el pivote salió en los minutos finales del partido ante el Inter para tratar de anestesiar un partido que amenazaba con aguar el estreno continental de los blancos. Tchouaméni salió al césped del Bernabéu para ocupar el lugar de Trent, al que Mou alineó de inicio en el centro del campo ante las bajas por sanción de Arda, Bernardo y Camavinga. El experimento del inglés no acabó de funcionar, y Mou acabó dando entrada al pivote más puro de la plantilla, una dinámica que se irá repitiendo de forma progresiva en los próximos partidos. Aurélien no está todavía para ser titular, pero sí para ayudar, especialmente en contextos tan complicados como el del pasado martes ante el Inter, que sometió al Madrid a un intenso cerco en busca de un empate que finalmente los blancos no concedieron. El regreso gradual de Tchouaméni es visto por Mou y su staff como la mejor noticia posible desde el punto de vista del equilibrio del equipo, huérfano hasta ahora de un especialista defensivo en el doble pivote. Bernardo, Fede y Camavinga tienen perfiles diferentes, más ofensivos que el ex del Mónaco, del que se espera aporte solidez al equipo una vez se complete su regreso a un óptimo nivel competitivo. A estas alturas, se trata sólo de una cuestión de tiempo que Tchouaméni sea uno más para Mou desde el punto de vista de la confección de los onces iniciales. Con él, el entrenador dispone de cuatro futbolistas de condiciones muy diferentes para confeccionar ese doble pivote que está siendo seña de identidad del equipo. Aurélien es el más defensivo y fuerte en los duelos de los cuatro, con Bernardo como el más creativo, Fede desde el dinamismo y la intensidad y Camavinga como opción más agresiva en la presión. A partir de ahora, Tchouaméni irá entrando de forma progresiva en los onces de Mou, que también dispone ya de la opción de Thiago Pitarch, un futbolista con capacidad para cubrir muchos metros. Con Arda destinado de momento a jugar unos metros por delante, estas cinco son las opciones de las que el técnico dispone para afrontar una temporada en la que la creación sigue ofreciendo de momento algunas dudas, a la espera de la recuperación total de todos los efectivos de la plantilla.

articles.title: La tarjeta negra llega al fútbol: Rumanía castigará a los padres que arruinen los partidos de niños
articles.standfirst: La medida llega para combatir los comportamientos abusivos en el fútbol formativo en torneos de formación comprendidos entre las categorías U7 y U16
articles.summary: La medida llega para combatir los comportamientos abusivos en el fútbol formativo en torneos de formación comprendidos entre las categorías U7 y U16
articles.body: La Federación Rumana de Fútbol (FRF) ha anunciado la introducción de la denominada tarjeta negra, una medida pionera destinada a combatir los comportamientos abusivos en el fútbol formativo. El organismo federativo asegura que se trata de una herramienta sin precedentes en el mundo del fútbol, creada específicamente para proteger a niños y adolescentes de las presiones, insultos y actitudes inadecuadas procedentes de las gradas. La nueva normativa ha sido aprobada este viernes, 11 de septiembre de 2026, por el Comité de Urgencia de la federación y entrará en vigor de forma inmediata desde la presente temporada en las competiciones de categorías inferiores. La medida será aplicable en los torneos de formación comprendidos entre las categorías U7 y U16, es decir, en el fútbol de niños y jóvenes. A diferencia de las tarjetas amarillas o rojas tradicionales, la tarjeta negra no está dirigida a los futbolistas. Su objetivo son los padres, familiares y espectadores que mantengan conductas consideradas abusivas o antideportivas durante los encuentros. La FRF considera que este tipo de comportamientos pueden afectar directamente al bienestar de los menores y perjudicar el desarrollo normal de los partidos. El protocolo contempla tres fases. En primer lugar, el árbitro interrumpirá temporalmente el juego y solicitará a los entrenadores que intenten calmar a sus aficionados. Si la situación persiste, el encuentro será suspendido durante 10 minutos y los equipos se retirarán a los vestuarios. Finalmente, si los incidentes continúan tras la reanudación, el colegiado mostrará la tarjeta negra y dará por terminado el partido de forma definitiva. Las consecuencias disciplinarias posteriores serán determinadas por la federación conforme a sus reglamentos Con esta iniciativa, la Federación Rumana de Fútbol pretende lanzar un mensaje contundente: el fútbol base debe ser un espacio de formación, diversión y aprendizaje, libre de insultos, intimidaciones o presiones ejercidas por los adultos. La tarjeta negra se convierte así en una nueva herramienta para garantizar un entorno más seguro y saludable para los jóvenes futbolistas. - Abuso verbal, mediante insultos o reproches, así como golpear o empujar a los propios hijos; - Insultar, golpear o empujar a miembros del personal de tu propio equipo; - Insultar, golpear o empujar a jugadores o miembros del personal del equipo contrario; - Desafiar constantemente, insultar, golpear o empujar a los árbitros y oficiales del juego; - Conflictos verbales o físicos con otros padres o espectadores.

articles.title: Juan Mata deja el Melbourne Victory mientras medita su futuro
articles.standfirst: El español medita ahora diferentes opciones y anunciar su retirada podría ser una posibilidad
articles.summary: El español medita ahora diferentes opciones y anunciar su retirada podría ser una posibilidad
articles.body: Juan Mata (Burgos, 1988) se 'marcha' del Melbourne Victory por la puerta grande. Se marcha, entre comillas, sí. El internacional español, campeón del mundo en 2010, ha decidido poner fin a su etapa como jugador del conjunto australiano, al que, sin embargo, continúa ligado por partida doble: no sólo es accionista, sino que, además, ocupa el cargo de presidente del comité de fútbol. “Disfruté cada minuto y me encantó todo lo que logramos la temporada pasada, volviendo a enamorarme del fútbol en un lugar tan especial, en una ciudad increíble a la que fue un privilegio llamar hogar", aseguró Mata, que la pasada temporada recibió la medalla Johny Warren al 'Mejor Jugador de la Liga' después de registrar cinco goles y ¡12 asistencias! en 25 partidos. “Ahora me entusiasman los próximos capítulos, creer juntos en el futuro e inspirar a la próxima generación de jugadores y aficionados del Melbourne Victory”, asegura Mata, que continúa meditando su futuro. ¿Significa su salida como jugador del Melbourne Victory que cuelga las botas? No necesariamente. A sus 38 años, después de pasar por Real Madrid Castilla, Valencia, Chelsea, Manchester United, Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe y Western Sydney Wanderers, es una opción que está meditando y lleva tiempo sobre la mesa. La decisión, sin embargo, no está tomada. Al menos, al 100%. Es cierto que le gustaría irse con un regusto dulce, pero si existe una propuesta que le seduzca -seguro que no le faltan-, podría continuar en activo. "Ahora concentrará su experiencia con el Victory en su puesto dentro del grupo propietario del club, mientras considera los próximos pasos en su carrera desde su hogar en Europa", asegura el comunicado del Melbourne Victory. Su, por ahora, último equipo le ha despedido por todo lo alto. "La temporada 2025-26 de Juan quedará grabada en la memoria de los aficionados del Victory y debería ser recordada con cariño por todos los seguidores del fútbol en Australia. Su rendimiento en el campo y su comportamiento dentro del club fueron ejemplares", subraya el director deportivo, John Didulica. “Le agradecemos todo lo que aportó y nos complace que, tras su decisión de unirse al Melbourne Victory, haya podido destacar dentro de la sólida cultura y el entorno de alto rendimiento que se han establecido aquí a lo largo de varios años. En el club estamos todos muy contentos de que forme parte de nuestro grupo propietario y, en el futuro, esperamos que su inteligencia futbolística lidere nuestro comité de fútbol", ha insistido Didulica.

articles.title: "Hay que plantarse: o la final es en España o nos retiramos"
articles.standfirst: José Manuel Oliván analiza en La Tribu el papel de Marruecos en la organización del Mundial 2030 y pide a España que se plante ante la FIFA
articles.summary: José Manuel Oliván analiza en La Tribu el papel de Marruecos en la organización del Mundial 2030 y pide a España que se plante ante la FIFA
articles.body: ricardo Reyes, José Manuel Oliván, Luz Monzón, Nacho Labarga, Selene Melián y Pepe Pasqués han sido los tertulianos de este viernes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar el estreno de Madring, el papel de Marruecos en la organización del Mundial 2030, y la actualidad de Real Madrid y Barcelona en la previa de una nueva jornada de Liga. José Manuel Oliván. "Desde que nació esta candidatura, hay una improvisación total y unos cambios tremendos. La FIFA está como está, es una auténtica anarquía. Hay que plantarse: reunirse, hablar y decir 'o la final es en España o nos retiramos'. Hay que tomar una decisión. No nos pueden estar toreando como nos están toreando". Ricardo Reyes. "¿Por qué no se firmó un documento, al recurrir a Marruecos, para mantener la final en España, en el Bernabéu? ¿Por qué no tenemos un papel firmado? Es una gran oportunidad para España, pero si vamos a organizar un Mundial y no tenemos ni la inauguración, ni la final y no va a ser el Mundial de España... nos vamos". Nacho Labarga. "Ahora mismo ni partido inaugural, ni final. La gente no tiene la sensación de que sea el Mundial de España". Luz Monzón. "En cuanto Julián marque dos goles, la situación cambia. Ante el Liverpool se le vio otra actitud, se vio un jugador diferente al que se vio en Liga. El juego del Barça hace que el Madrid vea más sus costuras y que haya más dudas". Pepe Pasqués. "La inversión del Atlético en el primer mercado de Apollo es menor a la que se hizo habitualmente estando Gil Marín al mando. El Barça está mostrando una superioridad importante. El Atleti, como dijo Simeone, está en construcción. Me sorprende que ya se esté cuestionando a Grimaldo. El Madrid tiene potencial para pelear mano a mano con el Barcelona". Selene Melián. "Ves al Barça y reconoces su patrón de juego. Las claves, la filosofía del club arraigada, la convicción sobre la manera de jugar y el acierto fichajes. Un equipo como el Real Madrid no se puede permitir el lujo de estar en construcción. El Atleti ha tenido un desgaste importante en las últimas temporadas: muchos partidos los pierde por el entrenador y no por el equipo".

articles.title: Realistic Upsets That Would Send the 2026-27 College Football Season into Chaos
articles.summary: Chaos hasn't really reared its wild-and-crazy head yet this season in college football, but there were Week 1 signs he was awakening from his slumber.
articles.body:
Chaos hasn't really reared its wild-and-crazy head yet this season in college football, but there were Week 1 signs he was awakening from his slumber.

Colorado upset Georgia Tech on the road. UMass followed up last year's winless season by beating Rutgers to open this year. But nothing totally earth-shattering happened.

Oregon shook off a scare from Boise. Louisville roared back against Ole Miss only to lose on a last-second field goal. The biggest avoided blunder came when Michigan (allegedly) beat Western Michigan on a last-second Hail Mary that's still being contested.

So, were there upsets? Sure. But nothing too, too shocking. Still, we all know it's just a matter of time, right? These would turn the sport on its head.

The Oklahoma Sooners are coming off a playoff showing a season ago and have aspirations of even bigger things this year as coach Brent Venables' program finally appears to be off and running.

Michigan has to block out all the noise and dodge the deserved strays from fans and media alike, as the Big Ten replay crew gave the Wolverines an extra second and an essential do-over Hail Mary last week to beat Western Michigan, 13-12.

Everything points to the Sooners winning on Saturday. But don't bet the house in the Big House.

Coach Kyle Whittingham has all the motivation he needs to light a fire under the Wolverines following a lackluster opener that still shows 1-0. There is plenty of talent on his roster. The Sooners haven't exactly displayed an offensive explosion with John Mateer under center.

This one could be closer than most expect. It would alter the season's trajectory for both powerhouse programs.

Before the Brendan Sorsby offseason gambling saga, Texas Tech was an almost lock pick for the College Football Playoff and an expected national title contender.

Whether they are or not, Will Hammond under center remains to be seen.

The Red Raiders are loaded essentially everywhere else, thanks to some shrewd recruiting and yet another massive transfer portal haul. They also have an extremely easy schedule, not even drawing Big 12 contenders like Utah or BYU on the schedule.

They do, however, host Willie Fritz's Houston Cougars in Lubbock in a couple of weeks, in a game where the visitors will be hungry to win. If they do, they could completely flip the script in the Big 12.

Fritz is a known program-builder. He has some incredibly nice pieces in Houston – enough to pull off the upset. The Red Raiders have a better roster, but if the Cougars can put pressure on Hammond, this one could get interesting.

SEC teams had better not sleep on South Carolina. If there's one sleeper team that could be lethal in shaking some trees out there, it's the Gamecocks.

Every week is a landmine in league play, so Coach Shane Beamer's team will have plenty of opportunities to do damage in the standings. They'll have to if he's going to keep his job.

This isn't the same team that won one league game last year. LaNorris Sellers is back under center. New offensive coordinator Kendal Briles has developed talent before. Sellers may have a better skill set than any of his previous field generals, too.

A season ago, they gave Alabama all it could handle in Columbia, losing 29-22. The Tide hosts them this year, as they have a better team. Beamer's bunch could be sneaky-strong, and it's early enough in the season to catch Kalen DeBoer's team by surprise.

Florida's first-game, 66-21 win over Florida Atlantic in the Swamp went largely overlooked on the national spectrum, but that was impressive considering the Owls were a popular pick to cover.

Instead, new quarterback Aaron Philo looked terrific. Running back Jadan Baugh looked like one of the top playmakers in the SEC. This is a dangerous team in coach Jon Sumrall's first year in Gainesville.

It's not like the Gators are devoid of talent. There is plenty of it there. If they get a little bit of confidence, watch out.

Some (including me) picked Ole Miss in the SEC championship game during the preseason, but there were plenty of red flags in the back two levels of Pete Golding's defense in a narrow win over Louisville to start the season.

Traveling to the Swamp after what is sure to be an emotional showdown when Lane Kiffin brings LSU back to Oxford, the week will be an interesting comeback-to-earth-and-refocus test for the Rebels. This one could easily swing the Gators' direction.

Let's not make any trigger-finger reactions to UCLA after its season-opening win over old Pac-12 foe California in Week 1. This team still has a long way to go to compete in the rugged Big Ten.

One thing is certain, though: The Bruins are a better team under first-year coach Bob Chesney. They're more disciplined, utilizing their talent and look more capable of going toe-to-toe with better foes.

When they go to Autzen Stadium in early October, the Bruins will have an opportunity to shock the world against a team many have pegged for the national championship.

The Ducks proved they were susceptible in the opener against a Boise State team that treated the showdown like a playoff game. It took a while for Oregon to match that intensity. Expect Chesney to have his team ready on the road.

He's much better equipped to compete than he was in last year's College Football Playoff as the coach of James Madison, but the Dukes played well then. UCLA will do the same this year.

There aren't many pitfalls on Notre Dame's football schedule, and very few things stand between the Fighting Irish and the College Football Playoff.

Not only do they have very few tough opponents; they've got a pretty loaded roster, too.

Of course, Miami (Nov. 7) and SMU (Nov. 21) will be tough outs, and North Carolina (Oct. 3) might be tougher than people expect. But an underrated-but-extremely tough test will come October 17 in Provo against BYU.

What if that game is at night? BYU is always tough to play in an absolutely raucous environment under the lights at LaVell Edwards Stadium. No matter where it is, though, the Cougars are going to be up and ready to play the Irish.

This is a national-spotlight team for coach Kalani Sitake's team, which has felt snubbed by the playoff committee in each of the past two years. This win would be a huge resume booster.

There have been a few years over the course of Pat Narduzzi's time at Pittsburgh, where elements of the Panthers roster made you think they could break out.

Of course, they haven't had a quarterback as talented as Mason Heintschel since Kenny Pickett. With Kade Bell calling plays, the Panthers are a dangerous opponent no matter who is standing on the other sideline.

Narduzzi always has a bunch of no-name recruits on defense that he turns into NFL stars. With the weapons Pitt has on offense, it's intriguing to see what the ceiling is.

They travel to Coral Gables in late October for what is almost certainly the game against the ACC's best opponent. With North Carolina and Notre Dame in the next two games, and rival Florida State before that, they could overlook Pitt.

That wouldn't be wise. This could be a shootout between the ACC's top two quarterbacks.

Ohio State looks loaded. Julian Sayin is a Heisman Trophy candidate. Jeremiah Smith is, too. Bo Jackson runs with reckless abandon. There are stars all over the defense.

Coach Ryan Day almost always has a couple of games a year where the Buckeyes don't look like the Buckeyes.

Their trip to Los Angeles to take on the Trojans is especially interesting. Yes, it comes after a bye, so that's good, but the week before that will be a heavyweight showdown with Indiana. The week after, Oregon comes to Columbus.

That's as tough a three-game stretch as any team in the nation faces.

USC's offense has explosive potential with Jayden Maiava leading the charge and a slew of young weapons on the perimeter.

The defense may not be quite good enough to battle for the Big Ten title yet, but if the game gets into a shootout, watch out. Lincoln Riley knows this is a national game that could reintroduce the Trojans to the national stage.

Virginia Tech had to feel like it had walked into a dream when Penn State fired James Franklin midway through last season. The way the coach had come into the Commonwealth and poached top talent for years, there was only one hire for the Hokies to make.

They made it, and now, the once-proud program has high expectations again.

This year, growing pains are expected. Franklin still brought in a lot of good players to flip the roster, led by quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer.

You can't make anything of a 73-3 season-opening win over VMI, but the Hokies are going to be better. In an ACC that looks somewhat open behind Miami, there's a lot of first-year goodwill to be earned.

SMU has playoff aspirations. With Kevin Jennings under center, the Mustangs should be explosive. A close win over Florida State proves they're beatable.

If the Hokies can beat them in November, it could knock the Mustangs out of the playoff and kick-start Franklin's program.

If you want a bold prediction after Week 1, the November 14 meeting between Texas and LSU will be for a spot in the SEC championship game.

The problem for the Longhorns and Tigers is that they can't overlook the week before. For LSU, it's a home game against Alabama. For the 'Horns, they have to travel to Missouri.

There's nothing exciting about CoMo in the winter. It's normally at least chilly at that time of year, with the wind whipping across the plains. It can wreak havoc on teams. It's a potential pitfall for anyone who goes there then.

Texas had better not overlook the game. Coach Eli Drinkwitz has been brutal in his career against ranked opponents (7-19 while at Mizzou), so the Longhorns have that on their side, but the Tigers have a capable quarterback in Austin Simmons.

By then, Ahmad Hardy will be back from his offseason gunshot wound and fully healthy. He's a load no matter who he's playing against. This game could be tougher than expected.

The Indiana Hoosiers are the defending national champion. They'll always be tough and disciplined as Curt Cignetti leads the way.

But they didn't look quite as invincible as you'd think at times during the season-opening win over North Texas. They still breezed through, 52-16, but it's going to be interesting to see if they're still the juggernaut they were last year after having to replace so many playmakers on both sides of the ball.

We'll know by this time late in the season, as the Hoosiers will already have faced several playoff-caliber opponents.

A cross-country trip to the Pacific Northwest at the tail end of the season, when a lot of the proverbial hay is in the barn, is an interesting test. By that time, the playoff picture will be sorting itself out.

Coach Jed Fisch's Huskies are expected to be a fringe possibility for the final 12. IU is definitely expected to be in. Could this game be an elimination game?

The Tennessee Vols aren't ready to be a playoff contender this year, in what is almost certainly a transitional season as they break in true freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon.

The immediate future is extremely bright, though, and by the end of the season, some of those lumps Brandon will take during the year will be ironing themselves out if he's healthy.

The Vols have a favorable home schedule this season with tough games against Texas, Alabama and LSU in Neyland Stadium. Coach Lane Kiffin's team comes in very late in the year. As much as UT fans detest Kiffin (get in line, right?), that's going to be a rowdy atmosphere.

Kiffin's Bayou Bengals look loaded on both sides of the ball, but there are a lot of things that can be clicking late in the year for Tennessee. Veteran defenders should know Jim Knowles' scheme inside and out, and, again, Brandon could be locked in.

LSU needs to be prepared for a war on Rocky Top.

articles.title: Tres partidos y 10 horas de avión en seis días
articles.standfirst: El Celta jugará este próximo miércoles en Chipre con solo una sesión para preparar el estreno europeo
articles.summary: El Celta jugará este miércoles en Chipre con solo una sesión para preparar el estreno europeo
articles.body: El Celta está plenamente centrado en preparar el encuentro de este domingo en Balaídos ante el Málaga pero ya son conocedores de que tendrán apenas una sesión de entrenamiento para preparar el debut de esta temporada en Europa League ante el Omonia Nicosia y menos de tres días antes de un tercer encuentro. El equipo de Claudio Giráldez concluirá su encuentro liguero del domingo entorno a las 16.00 horas y menos de 75 horas después ya estará debutando, esta temporada, en Europa League. En principio está prevista jornada de descanso para el lunes y el martes el equipo ha optado por entrenar en la Ciudad Deportiva Afouteza debido a la larga duración del viaje a Chipre, cercana a las 5 horas. Por ello tras la sesión de entrenamiento se desplazarán al aeropuerto de Peinador para partir a las 12.45, la llegada está prevista para cerca de las 19:00 hora local, al haber una hora más de diferencia con respecto a España. Ya en el estadio del encuentro, Claudio Giráldez ofrecerá la rueda de prensa oficial previa al partido. Tras el debut europeo, el Celta tampoco tendrá mucho tiempo para preparar la visita del Racing de Santander a Vigo ya que la misma tendrá lugar el sábado, menos de 70 horas después de la finalización del partido ante el Omonia Nicosia y con, igualmente, un largo viaje de vuelta desde Chipre. Tres encuentros en seis días y con diez horas de avión, eso es lo que le espera al Celta la próxima semana. Todo ello después de haber ya disputado cinco jornadas ligueras, desde el debut el pasado 22 de agosto en Mestalla. Los célticos afrontaron ya media decena de partidos en 16 días. Las múltiples rotaciones de Claudio Giráldez están teniendo más vigencia que nunca en este frenético arranque de temporada.

articles.title: Hull City's Sorba Thomas crashes outside training ground
articles.summary: Premier League winger Sorba Thomas's Land Rover overturns in Cottingham.
articles.body:
Premier League winger Sorba Thomas has been involved in a car crash close to Hull City's training ground, the club has confirmed.

The 27-year-old walked away from the crash, which happened on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham on Friday morning. His vehicle, a grey Land Rover Defender, was pictured on its roof, with broken windows.

Humberside Police said emergency services remained at the scene and asked people to avoid the area.

In a statement, the club said it was "relieved" to hear its player, who joined the Tigers from Championship side Stoke City earlier this month, was unharmed.

The club added: "The club is aware of images of Sorba's car circulating on social media and can reassure supporters that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed."

One NHS worker who lives on the road said the crash had left him unable to go to work.

"There will be patients who will miss appointments because of this," he said.

"It's one road in and one road out. It was an accident waiting to happen."

Thomas signed for an undisclosed fee at the end of the transfer window until summer 2030.

He represented Wales at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta: Arsenal manager says he deliberately sabotaged his team's travel plans to prepare for difficulties on the road
articles.summary: Arsenal were involved in travel difficulties on the way to Naples because of the UK Air Traffic Control incident on Tuesday; Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has revealed he has deliberately sabotaged the club's journey to stadiums, affected meal times and made changing rooms hotter
articles.body:
Those sabotages include deliberately making his team late for matches by changing their route or meal times - as well as making the changing room hotter and reducing the number of massage beds.

The Premier League champions had travel concerns during their trip to face Napoli in the Champions League this midweek, caused by the Air Traffic Control crisis on Tuesday.

Arsenal were due to fly out of Luton Airport at around 3pm UK time on Tuesday, but delays meant they arrived in the Italian city around three hours behind schedule.

When asked if his players were affected by that, Arteta revealed he prepared his players by creating difficult scenarios during pre-season games.

"I love those challenges. I try to create them in pre-season!" said Arteta. "So when they happen, we know how to experience them and we already know.

"Get to the stadium very late, change the routine so the players have to do something else. When it happens, and it can: the flight can be cancelled, or the train is delayed, there is so much traffic, I don't want the players and staff panicking.

"When that happens, adapt to it. We have two or three hours on the plane - can we use it? Play together, spend some time together, sleep.

"But don't complain or use it as an excuse because it's not helpful at all."

Asked what he has done, Arteta replied: "Just delaying the meals, delaying the transport, taking a different route. We've done many things.

"Make the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less [massage] beds. Those kinds of things because we're going to have to adapt to different contexts. And we will try to anticipate this and adapt to difficult conditions.

"When there's no element of surprise or stress on a matchday, I think it's important."

Pickpockets, lightbulbs - what else has Arteta done to Arsenal players?

Arteta gained similar headlines last year when it was revealed he tasked his former head of sports science and performance Tom Allen to hire a pickpocket to steal from his own players during an evening meal.

The pickpocket was disguised as a waiter during the meal - and after the dinner, Arteta held a pre-match team meeting where at the end, he presented his players' stolen items at the front of the room.

That ploy was in preparation for a match against a team who tried every possible tactic to gain an edge - and Arteta wanted to adopt a 'pickpocket mentality', to always be aware of people trying to steal advantages from them.

The Amazon Prime documentary All or Nothing also unveiled some more quirky Arteta tactics. Arsenal were due to play Liverpool at Anfield for the first time with fans back in the ground, so Arteta blasted out 'You'll Never Walk Alone' on loudspeakers during training, so his players could get used to the surroundings.

For another game, this time at home, Arteta also did a pre-match team talk involving a lightbulb - as he wanted his players to shine and emit energy and light to one another.

articles.title: Estados Unidos: un gigante amenazado
articles.standfirst: El rival de España en las semifinales del Mundial, dominador planetario, es el favorito pero...
articles.summary: El rival de España en las semifinales del Mundial, dominador planetario, es el favorito pero...
articles.body: Hay relatos que se explican perfectamente desde los datos. La tiranía absoluta impuesta por el baloncesto femenino de Estados Unidos es un caso perfecto. Sólo los números abruman: ocho oros olímpicos seguidos, cuatro Mundiales también consecutivos, casi 20 años sin perder un partido (el 21 de septiembre se cumplen), con un balance de 73-0 y acabar un Mundial con una media de 40 puntos de ventaja sobre sus rivales. Ningún otro deporte de equipo a nivel internacional, en chicos o chicas, ha mostrado semejante dominio de un país. El femenino sí es un Dream Team extendido en el tiempo. Cada equipo era casi mejor que el anterior, conformando una extraordinaria máquina de precisión para jugar al baloncesto que martilleaba una y otra vez sobre el rival. Ataques fugaces y mortales, físico incontestable, ritmo frenético y jugadoras con una calidad descomunal. Una hegemonía sin fisuras... hasta ahora. EEUU recibió el primer aviso serio en la final de los pasados Juegos en París 2024. Victoria agónica y para muchos injusta, 67-66 sobre Francia, en un partido que las galas supieron llevar a su terreno, sacando de su hábitat al gigante. Casi ganan y hubieran acabado con 18 años de dominio total. Las estadounidenses se salvaron en aquella ocasión y también ante Italia, hace pocos días, en el Mundial 2026. Segundo aviso y este más serio. Francia, entonces, era otra de las favoritas en sus Juegos, pero Italia no estaba en las quinielas a la hora de hablar de medallas. Las italianas lo tuvieron cerca, de nuevo embarrando el partido, llevando a las estadounidenses al terreno en el que se sienten más incómodas, cuando tienen que alargar posesiones, que es cuando mejor funciona el rigor táctico que no suelen tener. Las europeas ganaban a tres minutos para el final, 51-50 y perdieron 52-55 en otro partido a pocos puntos, con alguna que otra decisión polémica y con un intento triple sobre la bocina de Zandalasini para empatar. Son indudables señales de debilidad, de una fragilidad que no habían mostrado nunca. Es un escenario nuevo para jugadoras que en gran parte aún están saboreando sus primeros sorbos de experiencia internacional. Es un equipo fabuloso para remar con viento a favor, ha ganado muchos de sus partidos de forma muy holgada en Berlín, pero con muchas dudas y fisuras si el viento se vuelve en contra. Como pasó contra Italia. Cuando se hizo público el equipo que jugaría el Mundial, los expertos se fijaron más en las ausencias: Sabrina Ionescu, Kelsey Plum y, sobre todo, A'ja Wilson. Son bajas tremendas especialmente la de Wilson, la mejor jugadora del planeta hoy en día, la jugadora que, en caso de problemas, siempre está para sacar la basura. Esa figura indispensable no está en este 'Dream Team'. Al contrario, en el equipo que está en Berlín han surgido muchas incógnitas sobre el rendimiento de algunas jugadoras, especialmente en partidos igualados. Jackie Young es su mejor anotadora, 11 de media, con Napheesa Collier, 9,8 y Breanna Stewart por detrás, 9,5. La calidad de Caitlin Clark es indiscutible, al igual que la de Paige Bueckers, pero hay muchas dudas con otras jugadoras como Angel Reese, que para muchos no tendría sitio si hubieran venido todas, o Chelsea Gray, una de las veteranas, pero lejos de su prime. Pero la debilidad de EEUU no es tanto en el juego, que sigue siendo físico y a veces demoledor para su rival, como en la química. El equipo no parece unido, no se llevan bien, no es un ambiente que pueda ser capaz de repeler los malos momentos, al contrario, parece que han importado algunos de los males que se respiran en la propia WNBA. Si hay problemas, se absorben y se crean más problemas, no se repelen o se solucionan. Y ese desorden se nota en la pista. El equipo norteamericano también ha desmotrado que le sigue costando adaptarse a los torneos FIBA. Todos los equipos tienen su plan de entrenamientos por los horarios que les designaban, y los cumplían. A EEUU no le gustó el horario en un par de ocasiones, renunciaron a él y se buscaron un campo de entrenamiento alternativo. Lo han repetido para estas semifinales y en el día previo, no entrenan en el Uber Arena. Son los caprichos del gigante. Que a nadie le quepa duda que EEUU sigue siendo un extraordinario equipo. Es favorito ante España y si llega a la final, lo será también. Pero hay que pensar que las distancias, que hace años eran abismales, se han ido acortando, como pasa en los chicos. Tras el Mundial de Berlín la hegemonía puede continuar (o no) pero lo que quedará es que equipos como Francia o España están empezando a estar mucho más cerca del gigante. Falta saber si tanto como para derribarlo.

articles.title: Hidalgo elogia a Bordalás
articles.standfirst: "Nos tenemos que mirar en entrenadores como Bordalás", dijo el técnico del Deportivo en la previa del duelo ante el Getafe
articles.summary: "Nos tenemos que mirar en entrenadores como Bordalás", dijo el técnico del Deportivo en la previa del duelo ante el Getafe
articles.body: El Deportivo viaja a tierras madrileñas para enfrentarse a un Getafe que en el Coliseum es muy rocoso. Antonio Hidalgo elogió a su técnico, José Bordalás. "Soy un recién llegado a la categoría y Bordalás ha dirigido cientos de partidos en Primera. Ha conseguido muchas cosas. Los que venimos de abajo tenemos que mirarnos en entrenadores como él para seguir creciendo. Cada uno tiene su manera de ver el fútbol, pero esto va de sacar rendimiento y él lo hace siempre". El técnico catalán avisa que será un partido muy complicado y lleno de mini partidos de extrema dificultad. El Getafe siempre lleva al límite y los tres puntos serán muy disputados. "Es un partido con mucha dificultad. Un equipo que viene trabajando con una misma idea y el mismo entrenador mucho tiempo. Será complicado, con muchas situaciones de duelos, saben cómo quieren hacer su partido. Hay que estar concentrado en todas las disputas. Viene de hacer una campaña brutal el año pasado y eso habla del gran trabajo que hay detrás", comentó. El cuerpo técnico del cuadro gallego trata de llevar a la plantilla al trabajo diario y a no estar pendientes de la tabla clasificatoria. "Eso quiere decir que cada semana sumas. Siempre digo que esto va de sumar. Lo que da la diferencia es sumar de tres y con esa intención vamos. Pero con mucha humildad, porque esto es largo y hay que tener los pies en el suelo", concluyó.

articles.title: Enzo Maresca: Man City manager says "you need to adapt" to scheduling
articles.summary: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says teams "need to adapt" to the fixture scheduling as his side head into Sunday's derby with two days extra rest over rivals Manchester United.
articles.body:
Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says teams "need to adapt" to the fixture scheduling as his side head into Sunday's Premier League derby with two days extra rest over rivals Manchester United .

City won 2-0 at Porto in the Champions League on Tuesday evening, with United thrashing Sabah 4-0 a full 48 hours later - meaning Michael Carrick's side have less recovery and preparation time than their opponents.

But Maresca pointed to City's own situation from last September before facing Arsenal - when the Gunners played in the early kick-off at Athletic Club on Tuesday, while City faced Napoli in the 20:00 BST game on Thursday.

Last season, former boss Pep Guardiola joked he was taking his players "hiking in the mountains" in preparation for the game at Emirates Stadium.

When asked about the scheduling, Maresca told BBC Sport: "To be honest, the club mentioned to me that it happened exactly the same last year when the club played Napoli and then, after two days, played Arsenal .

"Sometimes it happens in football. I don't have any doubt that Man United are going to be ready for that. It just matters to adapt."

The expanded Champions League means teams now play two extra games in the group phase before the end of January, while English teams also have to contend with participating in the Carabao Cup.

City host Norwich in the third round next Thursday, while United play Brighton at Old Trafford the day before.

"I think that happens and you need to adapt," said Maresca, when asked if the scheduling equals itself out. "It happened last year with us, this season with them, next season it will happen with a different team."

Quizzed on how Carrick would be feeling, Maresca replied: "That's a question for Michael. The only thing I can say is it happened and you need to adapt."

Maresca takes charge of his first Manchester derby and has started the season with City in superb fashion, winning all three league games so far, while United have only managed to collect four points from their opening three games.

"It is very important for different reasons," said the Italian." We know how important a derby is, especially here. It is a special game.

"The most important thing we can do is try to be ourselves and then we see the final result."

articles.title: Joao Pedro, de olvidado por Ancelotti a 'MVP' de la Premier con Xabi Alonso: "Tiene ganas de triunfar"
articles.standfirst: El '9' del Chelsea ha sido elegido 'Mejor Jugador' del mes con dos goles y dos asistencias
articles.summary: El '9' del Chelsea ha sido elegido 'Mejor Jugador' del mes con dos goles y dos asistencias
articles.body: La ausencia de Joao Pedro (Ribeirao Preto, 2001) fue la que mayor controversia generó nada más conocerse la lista de Brasil para el Mundial. "Algunos de los jugadores que han estado con nosotros este año no estarán contentos con esta lista. Lo siento y quiero dar las gracias a todos los que han estado con nosotros. Sentimos mucho no incluir a Joao Pedro; su gran temporada en Europa merecía el puesto, pero debimos elegir a otro. Lo siento por él y por todos los demás", aseguró, a modo de disculpa, Carlo Ancelotti, que, sin embargo, no ha dudado en incluirle en la convocatoria para los dos próximos amistosos, ambos contra Australia. Méritos para estar en Canadá, EE.UU. y México, desde luego, había contraído. El ex del Brighton, fichado hace un año a cambio de 63,7 millones de euros, fue elegido 'Mejor Jugador' del Chelsea la pasada temporada después de registrar 20 goles, 15 en Premier, y nueve asistencias en 50 partidos (3.694'). Lejos de bajar los brazos, el ex de Fluminense y Watford, pretendido en su día por el Barcelona como sustituto de Robert Lewandowski, ha comenzado la temporada con ganas de reivindicarse. Su gran agosto le ha valido para ser elegido 'Jugador del Mes' en la Premier League. Marcó un gol y asistió en otro en el triunfo en el derbi sobre el Fulham (2-3) de Álvaro Arbeloa y volvió a marcar y asistir en la victoria contra el Brighton (4-3). Lo hizo, para más inri, con Ancelotti en la grada. "Intento hacer mi trabajo sin importar quién me esté mirando. Siempre busco mantener un alto nivel. En cuanto a la selección brasileña, quiero seguir haciendo mi trabajo y, si Dios quiere, estaré allí. Creo que he estado demostrando mi buen estado de forma a lo largo de los años. Tuve un buen comienzo la temporada pasada, y esta también; ahora se trata de mantener el ritmo", confesaba el brasileño a 'ESPN'. Mientras tanto, Xabi Alonso, que ya sustituyó a Ancelotti en el Real Madrid, confía en dar continuidad a su mejor versión en Stamford Bridge: "Tiene muchísimas ganas de triunfar. Joao está realmente decidido a tener una gran temporada. Viene de un gran año, en el que marcó muchos goles, y quiere seguir marcando cada vez más. Pero tenemos que ayudarle, porque por sí solo no es posible". Tiempo tiene. Acaba de renovar hasta 2034. "Siempre soñé con jugar en un gran club y el Chelsea cuenta con una larga tradición ganadora y grandes ambiciones para el futuro", admite Joao Pedro, que, nada más llegar, con el Mundial de Clubes ya en marcha, resultó decisivo: marcó dos goles a Fluminense (0-2) en semis y uno en la final contra el Paris Saint-Germain (3-0) para ayudar a los 'blues' a conquistar el título.

articles.summary: ESPN College GameDay began the 2026 season by heading to LSU last weekend to see the new-look Tigers take on Clemson.
articles.body:
ESPN College GameDay began the 2026 season by heading to LSU last weekend to see the new-look Tigers take on Clemson.

This week, the premier pregame show heads to another exciting college football destination for the biggest game of the week as #4 Texas hosts #1 Ohio State.

Texas is seeking more than just revenge after falling in the season opener to the Buckeyes last season: There are playoff hopes on the line.

When can fans check out the pregame action? Which team will emerge victoriously?

Crew: Rece Davis, Kirk Herbstreit, Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Nick Saban, "Sanford Steve" Couglin, Pete Thamel, Jen Lada, and Jess Sims

Texas welcomes No. 1 Ohio State to Austin, determined to earn redemption. Last season, the Longhorns entered Columbus as the top-ranked team in Week 1, but a 14-7 loss ultimately cost them a chance at an at-large College Football Playoff spot.

Heisman contender and projected top-five draft pick Arch Manning struggled in that game, completing 17 of 30 passes for 170 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. Now, with another year of experience against elite opponents, Manning is much better prepared for this high-stakes rematch. Since that defeat, he has guided Texas to a 4-1 record against ranked teams.

Meanwhile, Ohio State's quarterback Julian Sayin and star receiver Jeremiah Smith aim to ignite the Buckeyes' offense. Smith is widely regarded as the best receiver in college football, but Texas has successfully limited his impact with deep zone coverage, holding him to only 46 yards in two meetings.

Texas' revamped offensive line faces an early challenge, but with Manning's development and a defense that knows how to contain Smith, I predict Texas will edge out Ohio State in a thrilling finish and earn their first victory over a No. 1 ranked team since 2008.

articles.title: Inter Sticking with Under Fire New Top Goalie Martinez
articles.summary: Josep Martinez made a grave error early in the Real Madrid clash, turning the ball over while trying to take Federico Valverde on in the box, leading to a ve...
articles.body:
Josep Martinez made a grave error early in the Real Madrid clash, turning the ball over while trying to take Federico Valverde on in the box, leading to a very avoidable goal. However, he also denied Real Madrid's stars multiple times with monster saves afterward.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , Inter and Christian Chivu's trust in the goalie hasn't waned. He has been anointed as the starter in the summer after Yann Sommer 's contract wasn't re-upped. Ivan Provedel was brought in to serve as a reliable deputy, not necessarily to challenge the other option.

The backup will get some chances in a standard rotation, but Martinez will remain the no.1 for the foreseeable future. The coach praised his reaction, and the Spaniard has been impeccable so far, albeit with limited opportunities, during his two years at the club.

The ex- Genoa goalie is heavily relied upon for his ability with his feet, but that's where he's had some trouble, as he had a few close calls before the gaffe in the recent UEFA Champions League fixture.

They decided a few years back, since moving on from Samir Handanovic , that they didn't necessarily need a world-class shot-stopper to be successful, never truly investing in the role, and that comes with some consequences.

Conversely, they had overpaid to get him from Genoa, so they kind of had to eventually give him the starting job to justify that outlay. He's perfectly serviceable but has limited upside. It'd be a poor look if they lost faith at the first blunder. Still, he'll be under scrutiny for the whole campaign to decide whether he could be the top choice for a few years.

articles.title: Jakirovic named manager of the month for August
articles.summary: Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic has been named Premier League manager of the month for August.  The Tigers remain unbeaten in the league after the opening th...
articles.body:
Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic has been named Premier League manager of the month for August.

The Tigers remain unbeaten in the league after the opening three games of the season and sit third in the table with seven points.

They are also the only team yet to concede a goal in the top flight.

"I'm very happy and very proud," said Jakirovic to BBC Radio Humberside. "Being in company with all these great names and coaches is a great achievement for me.

"To win this is like a dream - somebody wake me up!

"I am very happy for all the people at the club, especially our players because without them this wouldn't be possible. This is also their award because they have shown everything on the pitch."

Jakirovic also joked that he doesn't believe in superstitions as it is often jested that the award carries a curse, which causes the winning manager's team to lose their next match.

"Two years ago, I got this award in August in Croatia and then they fired me in September!" he added. "So I have already broken this curse.

"I'm just looking forward to the next game of football. I don't care about superstitions."

The 49-year-old beat Arsenal's Mikel Arteta, Chelsea's Xabi Alonso and Manchester City's Enzo Maresca to the award.

articles.title: How UH decided on a SLAB entrance for the Cougars' football team. 'We needed to be Houston'
articles.summary: A red Cadillac, chrome swangas and a Lil' Flip soundtrack made UH's new pregame tradition one of college football's Week 1 talking points.
articles.body:
Smoke began filling the tunnel inside TDECU Stadium.

Lil' Flip's "The Way We Ball" provided the soundtrack.

A red Cadillac rolled down the tunnel, followed by the University of Houston football team.

For years, college football programs from coast to coast have searched for the perfect pregame entrance - something memorable, something unique, something that gets people talking.

"We needed to be different," said Alundis Pledge, UH's associate athletics director for fan engagement. "We needed to be Houston ."

This summer, UH's athletic marketing team began to research other pregame entrances, from Virginia Tech 's "Enter Sandman" to Oregon 's mascot Puddles riding a custom Harley-Davidson motorcycle.

For decades, the Houston-born custom-car tradition has been closely tied to the city's hip-hop culture.

SLAB is commonly said to stand for "slow, loud and bangin'."

"What other school in the country could do this?" Pledge said. "You know the SLAB cars are a Houston thing. This is going to set us apart."

You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter .

What happened next became one of the most talked-about moments from Week 1 of the football season.

"I loved what happened down in Houston," Pat McAfee said on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show." He added the rims "are classic Houston."

For Pledge and UH's marketing team, the entrance was the result of two months of brainstorming and research. They had been tasked to come up with something fresh that aligned with the rollout of the athletic department's "Built by Houston" campaign.

Pledge said "multiple concepts" were considered, including which song would accompany the entrance.

"This is what we landed on, and it stuck," Pledge said.

They looked at 16 different SLAB accounts and swanga makers on social media, searching for the right car and the right look before partnering with Texan Wire Wheels.

The 1979 Cadillac LeCab features 15-inch G20 wheels with signature 30-spoke chrome swangas hanging off the rims.

"The wheels are a big part of Houston culture," said John Davis, marketing director for Texan Wire Wheels. "It's a cornerstone for Houston culture, just as much as the UH Cougars are."

Some logistical concerns remained. School officials brought the car onto campus two or three times to see if it fit in the tunnel. Player safety was also a concern, along with any potential damage to the turf. Three extra patches of turf were placed to the left of the tunnel where the car could briefly park. "And we needed it to be red for first game," Pledge said.

Head coach Willie Fritz eventually signed off, giving the project the green light.

"Up until Monday, I wasn't 100% sure that we were actually going to be able to pull it off," Pledge said.

They did. The entrance quickly spread across social media.

"In a world of fakes, always be authentic," UH men's basketball assistant coach Kellen Sampson posted on X, formerly the website known as Twitter. FanSided included the SLAB entrance among its "Top 25 things you missed from a wild Week 1 in college football."

But UH wasn't taking anything for granted.

"We were fully prepared to have to pivot and try and go back to the drawing board after Game 1," Pledge said.

The SLAB will be part of UH's pregame entrance for the remaining five home games, including Saturday against Southern.

There could be a few surprises along the way, depending on the color of the Cougars' jerseys.

Night games should provide an even better backdrop, with the tunnel's red lighting adding to the effect.

Some UH players didn't even know the SLAB was coming until after they reached the field.

Running back Re'Shaun Sanford II said the SLAB and Houston "have the same vibe."

Latreveon McCutchin remembered the old entrance.

"I'm used to the little football helmet," the outside linebacker said of the motorized helmet that has been a feature on game days. "It's definitely a big upgrade."

articles.title: Hansi Flick counting on Barcelona veteran after long road back from injury
articles.summary: Andreas Christensen produced one of the most important individual performances in Barcelona’s 5-1 victory over Feyenoord.While the attention understandably w...
articles.body:
Andreas Christensen produced one of the most important individual performances in Barcelona's 5-1 victory over Feyenoord .

While the attention understandably went elsewhere, the Danish centre-back completed the entire match, which is a major milestone for a player whose recent career has been repeatedly interrupted by injury.

Now, according to SPORT , Hansi Flick is counting on Christensen as an important member of his squad now that the defender appears to have returned to full fitness.

It is a significant change from where the 30-year-old found himself only a few months ago.

Gone from fighting for fitness to starting in Europe

To understand the gravity of the defender's appearance, it is important to note that Christensen played more minutes against Feyenoord than he managed across the entirety of Barcelona 's Champions League campaign last season.

His 2025/26 European involvement amounted to just 77 minutes over four appearances, none of them starts. He played 30 minutes against Newcastle, eight against PSG , 33 against Chelsea and six against Eintracht Frankfurt .

This season already looks very different.

Andreas Christensen played full 90 minutes against Feyenoord. (Photo by Judit Cartiel/Getty Images)

Christensen completed Barcelona's pre-season and started two of their first three La Liga matches, against Elche and Rayo Vallecano , completing 90 minutes in both.

He then played just over 30 minutes against Valencia before returning to the starting XI against Feyenoord, which is enough to conclude that the consistency is finally returning.

The significance of that progress becomes clearer when looking back at last season.

On December 21, Christensen suffered a partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee during training.

The injury kept him out for more than 150 days, with his comeback eventually arriving on May 23 against Valencia.

That appearance came after more than five months without playing and consisted of 35 minutes.

Christensen has come a long way. (Photo by Judit Cartiel/Getty Images)

By then, much of his season had already disappeared.

Now, Christensen has been able to complete a full pre-season and build match fitness without another interruption. For Flick, that makes him a valuable option in a season where Barcelona will face a packed schedule.

Christensen is not just a defensive cover

Barcelona extended Christensen's contract until 2028 in July, another indication that the club values what he brings.

While his defensive reading is one part of it, his experience and ability to play out from the back give Flick another profile at centre-back, something that becomes particularly useful when the fixtures start arriving every few days.

Christensen is heading into his fifth season as a Barcelona player, but this feels like the beginning of a fresh chapter.

After spending much of the previous campaign trying simply to get back on the pitch, he is now being trusted with responsibility again.

articles.title: Bayern head into first-ever clash at Elversberg on the back of a strong run
articles.summary: A maiden encounter: At 17:30 CEST on Sunday evening, FC Bayern take on SV Elversberg for the first time in a competitive match. The 948th pairing in Bundesli...
articles.body:
A maiden encounter: At 17:30 CEST on Sunday evening , FC Bayern take on SV Elversberg for the first time in a competitive match. The 948th pairing in Bundesliga history has thrown up a clash of opposites. The record champions have played 2,080 matches in the top flight alone, whilst newcomers Elversberg have played just two so far. The municipality of Spiesen-Elversberg in the district of Neunkirchen has a population of around 13,000 while FCB, by contrast, has well over 430,000 members. However, following a sensational start to the season, SVE currently sit above the Munich side in the league – and so, once again, the truth will be revealed on the pitch on Sunday. Read on to find out what impressive statis Bayern have to offer against this surprise package.

SVE are Bayern's 57th opponents in the Bundesliga – the Munich side have won at least one game in the competition against each of the other 56 clubs. FC Bayern have in fact won all of their last ten maiden encounters – the most recent of eight defeats in first-time meetings like this (1-0) came in October 2000 at Energie Cottbus.

Although the recent 0–0 draw at Schalke wasn't the result Bayern had hoped for, it did at least mean their strong run continued: the record champions are now unbeaten in 27 Bundesliga matches away from home (20 wins, seven draws) – their last away defeat was a 2–1 loss to 1. FSV Mainz 05 in mid-December 2024. Bayern have only ever recorded one longer run of this type – between 2012 and 2014, they went 33 matches in a row without suffering defeat on the road.

More facts on the maiden clash in Elversberg

83 per cent – FC Bayern clearly dominated the game at Schalke. The Munich side enjoyed 83 per cent possession in Gelsenkirchen – FCB have recorded a higher percentage in the Bundesliga on just three occasions in the past 20 years.

46 attempts – SV Elversberg conceded the most shots on goal (46) on the first two matchdays, whilst FC Bayern conceded the fewest (15). Apart from Werder Bremen (48) at the start of the 2023/24 season, no team has faced as many attempts on goal in their first two matches in the past 16 years.

7 goals – SV Elversberg are the only Bundesliga newcomers, apart from MSV Duisburg (1963/64), to have scored seven goals in their first two matches in the top flight.

Six points – The last Bundesliga newcomers to pick up the full haul of points – as Elversberg have done – were TSG Hoffenheim in the 2008/09 season, after two matchdays.

98 Bundesliga goals – Harry Kane is still waiting for his first league goal of the season and continues to sit on 98 goals after 96 Bundesliga matches. The record for the fewest matches taken to reach the 100-goal mark in the Bundesliga is held by Dieter Müller (129).

No. 4 from the Saarland – Following Borussia Neunkirchen (3W/1D/0L), FC Homburg (4W/1D/1L) and 1. FC Saarbrücken (4W/2D/2L), SVE is the fourth club from the Saarland that FC Bayern will face in the Bundesliga. Whilst the fixtures in Munich have usually been one-sided affairs, the Saarland is the only federal state in which the record champions have a negative record (2 wins, 4 draws, 3 defeats in nine away matches there).

articles.summary: El técnico portugués del Levante consiguió superar, cuando dirigía al Benfica en la Youth League, en dos ocasiones a los catalanes
articles.body: Hay triunfos que te llevan al estrellato, y aquella Youth League le valió de mucho a Luís Castro para dar el salto definitivo al fútbol profesional. El Benfica juvenil, dirigido por aquel entonces por el actual técnico del Levante, superó en dos ocasiones al Barcelona en la edición de la 'mini champions'. Fue en la temporada 2021- 2022, competición en el que el conjunto portugués se alzó con el triunfo en la octava edición, superando al Red Bull Salzburg por un contundente seis a cero en la final. Gloriosos y culés quedaron encuadrados en el grupo E, junto a Bayern Munich y Dinamo Kiev, y en el que el Benfica concluyó la fase de grupos como líder, con un total de 15 puntos, tras conseguir cinco victorias y tan solo una derrota. Entre esos verdes, dos fueron contra el Barça. En la jornada dos, los lusos recibieron a los azulgranas de Fermín López, Marc Casadó y Akhomach, entre otros, y vencieron con rotundidad por cuatro tantos a uno. Ya en la segunda vuelta, en la quinta fecha, volvieron a superar a los azulgranas por cero goles a tres. Aquella campaña, tras conseguir el título continental, el equipo dirigido por Luís Castro se alzó con la intercontinental sub 20, venciendo en la final al Peñarol de Uruguay gracias a un solitario tanto de Luis Semedo. En toda su carrera, el actual técnico del Levante se ha enfrentado en tres ocasiones al Fútbol Club Barcelona. La última, en la jornada 25 del curso pasado, con derrota valenciana en el Camp Nou por tres a cero.

articles.title: Premier League: What is the KMI Panel and who is on it?
articles.summary: The Premier League introduced its Key Match Incident (KMI) Panel four years ago
articles.body:
The Premier League's Key Match Incident (KMI) Panel meets every week to dissect each major decision, from goals to penalties to red cards.

The KMI Panel was created by Premier League clubs in 2022 to take performance stats out of the hands of the refereeing body.

It is not intended to look at each incident like any fan or manager would. It takes into account the laws of the game and, crucially, how the Premier League expects its games to be refereed.

That is why the list of errors will not be as extensive as supporters would expect.

The KMI Panel first looks at the decision of the on-field referee team, then of the VAR.

As the VAR is operating to a higher threshold - clear and obvious - there are times the KMI Panel will say the referee was wrong but the VAR was correct not to intervene.

That might sound confusing, so think of it this way...

A referee gives a penalty, a decision which many might disagree with. Yet at the same time, some might also say "but I can see why he's given it". That is when you will get 'incorrect on-field, but not to the VAR threshold'.

The KMI Panel also considers second yellow cards which were missed, or incorrectly shown.

Results from the KMI Panel are released one week after the conclusion of each meeting, and roughly 10 days after the final match of the round.

The judgements are used into a couple of other ways, too.

Each incident comes with a difficult level, with the results used to create the merit table for Premier League referees.

In effect, it creates a performance table which determines each referee's salary bonus. The officials towards the bottom will only receive a minor additional payment.

The findings also help to identify areas for further discussion, such as the relaxation of the definition of red cards for hair-pulling for this season.

How does the KMI Panel remain impartial?

While the KMI Panel consists of five people, they are not the same people each week and are selected on a rotational basis.

The Premier League keeps the identities of those involved anonymous, but we do know that each panel consists has five members: three former players and coaches, plus one representative each from the Premier League and Professional Game Referees (Pro Ref).

By rotating who is involved each week, the Premier League feels that this helps to maintain impartiality across decisions.

In a similar fashion to the Premier League, the Scottish Football Association introduced their own Key Match Incident Review Panel in September 2024.

It was composed in similar fashion to the Premier League, with five members - three ex-coaches, former players and/or members of the Scottish football media, plus one representative from the Scottish FA and one from SPFL clubs.

But at the start of this season, the SFA opted to discontinue the KMI Panel . This was due to clubs withdrawing from sending representatives to be involved in the reviews.

Dundee United were the first to pull out in February 2025, citing concerns over the panel's "purpose, effectiveness and impact on Scottish football".

The Tannadice club said "the panel's outcomes have been inconsistent with feedback provided by the Scottish FA". That was a reference to the monthly reviews by the SFA head of refereeing Willie Collum, who often disagreed with the panel.

Other clubs are believed to have followed United's lead from the process ahead of the start of this season.

articles.title: Matteo Moretto desvela la oferta que rechazó Camavinga: "El Galatasaray estaba dispuesto a pagar 50 millones"
articles.standfirst: El periodista cuenta en La Pizarra que el Real Madrid escuchó ofertas por el francés, pero el centrocampista quiso quedarse y "se ganó la confianza de Mourinho"
articles.summary: El periodista cuenta en La Pizarra que el Real Madrid escuchó ofertas por el francés, pero el centrocampista quiso quedarse y "se ganó la confianza de Mourinho"
articles.body: Matteo Moretto repasó en La Pizarra algunos de los movimientos que no terminaron produciéndose durante el mercado y adelantó varios nombres que podrían volver a ser protagonistas en los próximos meses. Entre ellos aparece Eduardo Camavinga, por quien el Galatasaray estuvo dispuesto a realizar una importante inversión. "Durante el verano, había un club turco, el Galatasaray, que estaba dispuesto a pagar 50 kilos por Camavinga", desveló Moretto. El periodista explicó que el intento no prosperó por decisión del propio futbolista: "El Galatasaray intentó ficharle, pero Camavinga lo rechazó, quiso quedarse en el Madrid". Además, Moretto señaló que el Real Madrid sí estuvo dispuesto a estudiar una posible salida: "El club escuchó ofertas por él, pero el jugador se ganó la confianza de Mourinho". Otro de los nombres propios de la intervención fue Anthony Martial. "Veremos si el Málaga va a fichar a Martial. Hay negociaciones en curso, buena predisposición por parte del futbolista, su mujer quiere vivir en España, quiere volver a España. Martial queda libre y está en conversaciones con el Málaga", aseguró. Moretto añadió que el apartado económico no debería ser el principal obstáculo: "No será un tema económico, porque se va a bajar la ficha, va a hacer esfuerzo por jugar en España". El Málaga maneja también otra posibilidad: "Hay otro nombre sobre la mesa. De momento es un sondeo: Wilfried Zaha, otro ex United, otro extremo. De momento Martial es la opción más factible, pero también Zaha podría ser una idea". El periodista también puso el foco en Joselu y su posible regreso a LaLiga durante el mercado invernal. "Lo normal es que se quede libre, que siga entrenando para volver a España. En enero tiene muchas posibilidades de volver a LaLiga". Según Moretto, varios clubes ya se interesaron por su situación: "Hubo muchos equipos españoles que preguntaron por él: Alavés, Getafe, Sevilla sobre todo, y dos más. El Valencia también preguntó". Aunque ninguna operación salió adelante, dejó una previsión clara: "En enero algo va a pasar y en España". Moretto reveló también un movimiento del Barcelona por Ruud Nijstad, central zurdo del Twente. "El Barça estaba buscando un central zurdo de proyección y Nijstad es muy bueno. El Barcelona lo intentó hasta el último día. Tenían un acuerdo de palabra con el futbolista, él estaba loco por fichar por el Barça, pero el Twente y su entrenador no abrió las puertas a esa posibilidad. Seguirá siendo un nombre de cara a futuro para el Barça", añadió. Sobre Raphinha, Moretto aseguró que las conversaciones con el Barcelona para ampliar su contrato llevan tiempo en marcha: "Están hablando desde hace meses, creo que acabará renovando". Además, recordó que "tuvo la posibilidad de irse a Arabia pero no quiso y el club tampoco" y apuntó que "Flick está enamorado de Raphinha". Por último, Moretto señaló que Rodrygo Goes "debería estar disponible a partir de diciembre", mientras que Eder Sarabia tuvo una opción en Grecia: "Tuvo la posibilidad de irse a Grecia, a Olympiacos, era una de las primeras opciones, pero Sarabia quiso esperar, está esperando cuál podría ser el proyecto adecuado".

articles.title: Cody Gakpo injury update revealed before Liverpool face Fulham
articles.summary: Bradley Barcola is expected to be available after he was removed late on against Atletico Madrid due to cramp
articles.body:
Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo is a doubt to face Fulham on Saturday but Andoni Iraola expects Bradley Barcola to be available to make his full Premier League debut following his late substitution against Atletico Madrid in midweek.

Gakpo was close to leaving Liverpool in the summer but the 27-year-old has started the season in excellent form, assisting all three of Alexander Isak 's goals in the Premier League, including both in the 2-1 win at Ipswich last Friday.

The Netherlands international was ruled out of Wednesday's Champions League win over Atletico due to "adductor issues", however, after feeling discomfort on both sides following the win at Portman Road last week.

It meant Barcola made his first start for Liverpool since his big-money move from Paris Saint-Germain and the winger impressed with a bright showing before he was removed late in the match due to cramp.

Liverpool will assess both players following training on Friday and Iraola said: "Barcola was just cramps. We have to evaluate how he is today, but there is no injury. I think he should be available if everything goes normal.

"Cody we will see. We will try today and see if he is ready for tomorrow or if we need to wait until the next one."

Iraola remains unbeaten in his first four games at Liverpool and the Reds arrive into Saturday afternoon's meeting with Fulham after back-to-back wins over Ipswich and Atletico, but the Basque also believes there is still lots of improvement.

Iraola's side have scored two goals in all four of their games so far and he said: "The team has goals in it. In all of the games we have been dangerous and created chances, we have scored two [in the last two] and could have scored more. Now it's about being more efficient.

"So not conceding the two goals against Newcastle, not conceding the two goals against Forest. It's also when the goals come because I don't think we're starting games too well. We [started well against] Ipswich and the games look more comfortable when you start like this.

"I would like to score the fist goal to make things easier, but we have to have the right mentality. We didn't start badly against Atletico but I think the start of games is one of the parts where I think we can be a bit better. I want us to impose ourselves from the beginning."
